technique: 3DM CAD model viewer with layer visibility controls
description: Renders a Rhino 3DM CAD/architectural model in a 3D scene with orbit navigation and a layer panel that toggles geometry visibility by layer name. Suits architecture, product design, or engineering portfolio sites that need to display professional CAD models directly in the browser.
usageNote: Wrap the renderer setup and loader call inside a useEffect with a canvas ref; assign renderer.domElement to the ref instead of appending to document.body. Replace the local 'models/3dm/Rhino_Logo.3dm' path with a URL to your own .3dm file (CDN, /public folder in Next.js, or an API route). The Rhino3dmLoader requires a CDN-hosted rhino3dm WASM library via setLibraryPath—keep that CDN call or self-host the WASM files. For react-three-fiber, use a custom loader hook with useLoader or manual useEffect to call Rhino3dmLoader since it is not natively supported by drei. Dispose the scene and renderer in the useEffect cleanup function.
constraints: Requires WebGL renderer; loads a large WASM binary (~5 MB) from CDN on first use which adds significant initial load time. Not suited for performance-critical mobile experiences or pages where 3DM assets are unavailable. The Z-up coordinate convention (DEFAULT_UP set to 0,0,1) affects the whole scene and may conflict with other Three.js objects that assume Y-up.
antiPatterns: Forgetting to dispose the Rhino3dmLoader WASM module and scene objects on component unmount causing memory leaks; not handling the loading spinner or progress state in React; hardcoding window.innerWidth/innerHeight instead of using the container element's dimensions; mutating THREE.Object3D.DEFAULT_UP globally which breaks other scenes rendered in the same session; not awaiting WASM readiness before attempting a second load.
accessibilityNotes: The 3D canvas is not keyboard-navigable by default; add an aria-label to the canvas element describing the model. Provide a static screenshot or image fallback for users with reduced motion or no WebGL support. OrbitControls are mouse/touch driven—consider adding keyboard shortcuts or describing the model content in surrounding HTML for screen reader users. GUI layer toggles should be mirrored as accessible HTML checkboxes if the layer panel is a primary UI feature.

technique: interactive 3DS model viewer with trackball orbit controls
description: Renders a fully textured and normal-mapped 3D model loaded from a legacy .3DS file, with ambient and directional lighting and free 360-degree mouse-drag rotation. Suits product showcase pages, portfolio sites, game asset previews, or any e-commerce or marketing section that needs an interactive 3D prop viewer.
usageNote: In React/Next.js, initialise the renderer inside a useEffect with a cleanup function that calls renderer.dispose() and removes the animation loop. Attach the renderer to a ref'd <canvas> or div rather than document.body. Replace local asset paths (the .3ds file, texture folder, and normal map) with paths served from your /public directory or a CDN URL. In react-three-fiber, use useLoader with a custom TDSLoader factory and <primitive object={…} /> to integrate the loaded object into the JSX scene graph.
constraints: Requires WebGL support; not suitable for very low-end mobile GPUs due to normal mapping and multi-texture overhead. The TDSLoader is a legacy format parser and may not support all 3DS features. Full-screen canvas is fine for hero sections but needs containment CSS if used in a card or panel layout. Normal maps must be supplied separately as .3DS does not embed them.
antiPatterns: Forgetting to dispose the renderer, geometry, and textures on component unmount causes GPU memory leaks in SPAs. Hardcoding window.innerWidth/innerHeight instead of using the container element's dimensions breaks embedded layouts. Failing to set setResourcePath before load will silently drop textures. Not updating camera.aspect and calling updateProjectionMatrix on resize causes distortion.
accessibilityNotes: Provide a static fallback image of the model for users with prefers-reduced-motion or no WebGL support. The interactive canvas is not keyboard-navigable by default; add tabIndex and keyboard event handlers (arrow keys for rotation) for accessibility. Include an aria-label on the canvas element describing the 3D object shown. For screen readers, add visually-hidden descriptive text about the model near the canvas.

technique: photorealistic 3D globe tile streaming with volumetric clouds and atmospheric perspective
description: A photorealistic Earth view streaming real-world 3D city tiles (via Cesium Ion) beneath physically accurate volumetric clouds, atmospheric scattering, and dynamic sun lighting. Ideal for hero sections of mapping products, satellite imagery platforms, geospatial analytics dashboards, travel or logistics apps, or any product that wants a dramatic 'view from above' establishing shot.
usageNote: Wrap the entire init() call inside a React useEffect with a canvas ref, returning a cleanup function that disposes the renderer and tiles. Replace the global renderer.domElement append with renderer.domElement assignment to the ref. The Cesium Ion API key must be stored in an environment variable (NEXT_PUBLIC_CESIUM_ION_KEY). The postprocessing, @takram/three-clouds, @takram/three-atmosphere, and @takram/three-geospatial packages must be installed and added to the import map or bundler aliases. React-three-fiber is not recommended here due to the custom tile renderer and postprocessing pipeline; raw Three.js inside useEffect is the safer path.
constraints: Extremely high GPU cost: volumetric clouds, cascaded shadow maps, atmospheric scattering, and tile streaming all run simultaneously. Requires WebGL2 and HalfFloat render targets. Not suitable for mobile or low-end devices. Requires an active Cesium Ion account and API key for tile data. Network-heavy due to streaming 3D tile assets. Minimum 8 GB VRAM recommended for smooth performance.
antiPatterns: Forgetting to call tiles.dispose() and controls.dispose() on component unmount will cause memory leaks. Hardcoding window.innerWidth/innerHeight instead of using the container element dimensions will break in embedded or non-fullscreen layouts. Omitting the resize listener will leave the camera aspect ratio and renderer size stale. Not rotating API keys before shipping to production. Failing to handle the async init() rejection if Cesium Ion auth fails.
accessibilityNotes: Provide a high-quality static image fallback (a satellite photo of the focal region) for users with prefers-reduced-motion or on devices that fail the WebGL capability check. Add an aria-hidden='true' attribute to the canvas and expose meaningful textual content about the location in the surrounding DOM for screen readers. Keyboard navigation is unsupported in the default GlobeControls; add tab-focusable UI controls if the globe must be interactive for all users.

technique: interactive 3MF model viewer with orbit controls and material support
description: Renders a fully colored and textured 3D model loaded from a .3MF file, centered automatically in the viewport with orbit controls for rotation and zoom. Ideal for product pages, e-commerce listings, medical device showcases, or 3D-printable part catalogs where users need to inspect a physical object from all angles.
usageNote: Wrap the renderer setup inside a useEffect with a canvas ref in React/Next.js; attach renderer.domElement to the ref instead of document.body. Replace the 'models/3mf/' local asset paths with URLs pointing to your own CDN or API route that serves .3mf files. Use a cleanup function in useEffect to dispose the renderer and remove event listeners. react-three-fiber is also viable but the ThreeMFLoader must still be used imperatively via useLoader or a custom hook.
constraints: Requires WebGL 1 or 2; 3MF files can be large and complex so load time and GPU memory scale with model polygon count and texture size. Mobile support is generally good but high-poly models may cause frame drops on low-end devices. The format natively supports multi-material and vertex/face color data, making it best suited for manufacturing or medical visualization contexts rather than purely decorative use.
antiPatterns: Forgetting to dispose geometry, materials, and textures when swapping models causes GPU memory leaks—the existing traversal disposal pattern must be preserved. Hardcoding window.innerWidth/innerHeight instead of the container element's dimensions breaks layout in non-fullscreen contexts. Omitting controls.update() after camera changes can cause stale view states. Not setting camera.up to (0,0,1) will misalign models authored with Z-up conventions typical of 3D printing tools.
accessibilityNotes: Provide a static fallback image of the model for users with reduced motion preferences or no WebGL support. Add aria-label to the canvas element describing the product shown. Keyboard navigation is not natively supported by OrbitControls; consider adding keyboard shortcuts for rotation increments. Screen readers cannot interpret 3D scenes, so pair the viewer with descriptive text content.

technique: 3MF model viewer with orbit controls and shadow casting
description: Renders a fully lit, shadow-casting 3D model loaded from a .3mf file on a neutral grey ground plane with fog depth, allowing the user to orbit around it freely. Ideal for product pages, e-commerce detail views, engineering or manufacturing showcases, and 3D printing service platforms where customers need to inspect a physical object interactively.
usageNote: Wrap the init logic inside a useEffect with a canvas ref in React/Next.js; pass the ref's current element to the WebGLRenderer constructor instead of appending to document.body. Replace the hardcoded './models/3mf/truck.3mf' path with a URL to your own .3mf asset hosted on a CDN or served from /public in Next.js. Clean up by calling renderer.dispose() and controls.dispose() in the useEffect return. Alternatively, use react-three-fiber with @react-three/drei's useGLTF or a custom loader hook, but the ThreeMFLoader must still be imported from three/addons.
constraints: Requires WebGL 1 or 2; works on most modern mobile browsers but shadow mapping and high-res .3mf parsing can be expensive on low-end devices. The 3MF format supports multi-material and multi-component meshes, so file size and parse time can be significant. Not suitable for scenes requiring many simultaneous models without instancing or LOD strategies.
antiPatterns: Forgetting to call renderer.dispose() and remove the resize event listener on unmount causes memory leaks in SPAs. Hardcoding window.innerWidth/innerHeight instead of reading the container element's dimensions breaks embedded viewers. Not calling controls.update() after changing the target causes the camera to snap. Omitting the z-up rotation correction (object.rotation.set(-Math.PI/2, 0, 0)) will display 3MF models lying flat.
accessibilityNotes: The canvas has no accessible label by default; add an aria-label or role='img' with a descriptive title on the canvas element. Provide a static fallback image for users with prefers-reduced-motion or when WebGL is unavailable. Keyboard users cannot orbit without additional key-event bindings on OrbitControls; consider adding arrow-key support or a visible UI for rotation. Screen readers receive no information from the canvas; supplement with a text description of the displayed object.

technique: interactive 3D model viewer with orbit controls (AMF format loader)
description: Renders a textured or multi-material 3D solid model on a neutral grid background with orbit-controlled camera rotation, suited for product pages, 3D printing service configurators, engineering part catalogs, or e-commerce sites that need to display manufacturable objects interactively.
usageNote: Wrap initialization in a useEffect with a canvas ref: create the renderer targeting the ref element instead of appending to document.body, and clean up renderer, controls, and event listeners on unmount. Replace the hardcoded './models/amf/rook.amf' with an AMF file hosted in your public folder or a CDN URL (e.g. '/models/part.amf' in Next.js public/). In react-three-fiber use a custom useLoader hook or a Suspense-wrapped loader component to handle the AMFLoader asynchronously.
constraints: Requires WebGL support (broadly available). AMF is a niche format used primarily in 3D printing workflows; most web assets will need conversion to glTF/GLB instead. Performance is low-cost for single-mesh models but can be moderate for large multi-material AMF files. Mobile support is fine but orbit controls need touch event consideration. Not suited for scenes requiring many simultaneous model instances.
antiPatterns: Forgetting to call renderer.dispose() and controls.dispose() on component unmount causing memory leaks; hardcoding window.innerWidth/innerHeight instead of measuring the container element; not updating camera.aspect on resize; neglecting to remove the resize event listener; assuming AMF files will retain colors without checking the loader output for material groups.
accessibilityNotes: Provide a static fallback image of the model for users with prefers-reduced-motion or no WebGL support. Add an aria-label to the canvas element describing the model. Keyboard users cannot orbit by default — consider adding keyboard-driven camera controls or a text description of the object as supplemental content. Screen readers receive no spatial information from the canvas.

technique: BVH skeletal animation playback with wireframe skeleton helper
description: A wireframe stick-figure skeleton plays a looping motion-capture animation (e.g. a pirouette) rendered over a neutral grid floor. Suits interactive portfolio sites, dance/movement studios, fitness apps, game character preview pages, or any product that needs to showcase human motion data or character rigs.
usageNote: In React/Next.js, initialize the renderer and loader inside a useEffect with a canvas ref, returning a cleanup function that calls renderer.dispose() and cancels the animation loop. With react-three-fiber use a useLoader hook or manual fetch inside useEffect. Replace the local .bvh asset path with a URL pointing to your own hosted BVH file (CDN, public folder, or API route); BVH files are plain text and can be served statically.
constraints: Requires WebGL renderer; not suitable for server-side rendering without a canvas stub. BVH animation is CPU-light and GPU-light — runs well on mobile. AnimationMixer update must be called every frame; frame-rate-dependent logic will break if delta is not used. Large BVH files with many bones or very long clips may spike load time but runtime cost stays low.
antiPatterns: Forgetting to call mixer.stopAllAction() and mixer.uncacheRoot() on unmount causes memory leaks. Not removing the resize event listener on cleanup. Hardcoding window.innerWidth/innerHeight instead of measuring the container element breaks embedded/partial-page layouts. Forgetting to disconnect the Timer from the document on cleanup.
accessibilityNotes: Respect prefers-reduced-motion by pausing or stopping the mixer when the media query matches. Provide a static screenshot or poster image as a fallback for users who have disabled motion or whose devices do not support WebGL. The canvas element should have a descriptive aria-label (e.g. 'Animated skeleton demonstrating a pirouette motion capture sequence') and role='img' since it conveys no interactive content.

technique: rotating 3D character model loaded from Collada (.dae) file
description: A textured 3D character model slowly rotates in place under ambient and directional lighting, creating a turntable presentation effect. Ideal for product showcases, game character previews, NFT or avatar displays, and portfolio sites that need an interactive 3D mascot or hero element.
usageNote: In React or Next.js, wrap all Three.js setup in a useEffect with a canvas ref and return a cleanup function that calls renderer.dispose() and cancels the animation loop. For react-three-fiber, use useLoader with ColladaLoader and a useFrame hook for rotation. Replace the hardcoded './models/collada/elf/elf.dae' path with a URL pointing to your own .dae asset hosted in /public or on a CDN; Collada files often reference external textures so keep relative paths intact or bundle textures alongside the .dae file.
constraints: Collada (.dae) is a verbose XML format with potentially large file sizes; prefer glTF/GLB for production use if asset authoring allows it. WebGL renderer required — no WebGPU or CSS fallback. Moderate GPU cost for complex meshes. Mobile supported but frame rate may drop on low-end devices with high-poly models.
antiPatterns: Forgetting to dispose renderer, geometry, and materials on component unmount causing memory leaks in SPAs. Not handling the async loading lifecycle (model undefined errors if render fires before load completes). Hardcoding window.innerWidth/window.innerHeight instead of measuring the container element, which breaks embedded or partial-page layouts. Neglecting to co-locate Collada-referenced texture files, causing broken materials silently.
accessibilityNotes: Add a prefers-reduced-motion media query check and stop the rotation animation (set delta multiplier to 0) when reduced motion is preferred, leaving the static model visible. Provide an aria-label on the canvas element describing the 3D model for screen readers. Consider a static fallback image for environments where WebGL is unavailable, detected via a try/catch on WebGLRenderingContext.

technique: animated articulated robot arm with COLLADA kinematics and smooth joint tweening
description: A multi-joint industrial robot arm loads from a COLLADA file and continuously animates its joints through randomized poses using smooth easing tweens, with a slowly orbiting camera. Suits manufacturing, automation, robotics product, or engineering firm websites to showcase mechanical precision and technical sophistication.
usageNote: In React/Next.js, wrap all scene setup inside a useEffect with a canvas ref, returning a cleanup function that calls renderer.dispose() and cancels the animation loop. Replace the ColladaLoader path with a URL to your own .dae file hosted in /public or via a CDN — the local asset path './models/collada/abb_irb52_7_120.dae' will not exist and must be substituted. With react-three-fiber, use useLoader(ColladaLoader, url) and manage the kinematics tween in a useEffect or useFrame hook.
constraints: Requires WebGL renderer with antialias support; COLLADA parsing is CPU-intensive at load time and may be slow on low-end mobile devices. The kinematics system depends entirely on the loaded .dae file containing valid kinematics data — not all COLLADA files include this. Not suitable for pages requiring instant first paint or where 3D assets are unavailable.
antiPatterns: Forgetting to call renderer.dispose() and remove the animation loop on component unmount causing memory leaks; not handling the asynchronous COLLADA load before calling init(); hardcoding window.innerWidth/innerHeight instead of using the parent container dimensions; not replacing the local asset path with a valid hosted URL; omitting the TWEEN.update() call in the animation loop which breaks all joint animations.
accessibilityNotes: Provide a static high-quality render or product image as a fallback for users with prefers-reduced-motion enabled or for screen readers using aria-hidden on the canvas. Add an aria-label to the container describing the robot arm visualization. The orbiting camera and continuous joint motion should be paused or replaced with a still pose when reduced motion is preferred.

technique: skeletal-animated 3D character viewer with Collada skinning and orbit controls
description: A fully skeletal-animated 3D humanoid character plays a looping animation on a grid floor with ambient and directional lighting, viewable from any angle via mouse/touch orbit. Suits product pages for games, character creators, avatar selection screens, entertainment portals, or any site showcasing rigged 3D characters or creatures.
usageNote: Wrap initialization in a useEffect with a canvas ref and return a cleanup function that calls renderer.dispose() and removes the animation loop. Use react-three-fiber alternatively for cleaner lifecycle management. Replace the hardcoded './models/collada/stormtrooper/stormtrooper.dae' path with a URL to your own .dae file hosted on a CDN or served from /public in Next.js. OrbitControls and ColladaLoader must be imported from 'three/addons' and included in your import map or bundler aliases.
constraints: Collada (.dae) skinned meshes can be CPU-intensive to parse and animate; complex rigs with many bones may drop frames on low-end mobile. Requires WebGL (not WebGPU). The ColladaLoader does not support all DAE authoring tool exports equally — prefer FBX or glTF/GLB for broader compatibility and smaller file sizes. Best suited for hero sections rather than repeated instances.
antiPatterns: Forgetting to call mixer.stopAllAction() and mixer.uncacheRoot() plus renderer.dispose() on component unmount causes memory leaks. Hardcoding window.innerWidth/innerHeight breaks in embedded or multi-panel layouts — use the container element's dimensions instead. Not handling the async load callback before component unmount can cause state-update-on-unmounted-component errors in React.
accessibilityNotes: Wrap the canvas in a region with aria-label describing the character and its animation. Respect prefers-reduced-motion by pausing the AnimationMixer (mixer.timeScale = 0) and showing a static poster image instead. Provide keyboard-accessible orbit controls or a static fallback image for screen reader users who cannot interact with the 3D view.

technique: Draco-compressed 3D mesh viewer with orbiting camera and spotlit scene
description: A single high-detail 3D mesh (e.g. a product, character, or sculptural object) loaded from a Draco-compressed file is displayed on a softly lit ground plane with fog and a slow orbiting camera, creating a showcase feel. Ideal for product detail pages, portfolio spotlights, or hero sections that need to display complex geometry efficiently without sacrificing visual quality.
usageNote: In React/Next.js, wrap the initialization logic in a useEffect with a canvas ref and return a cleanup function that calls renderer.dispose() and dracoLoader.dispose(). With react-three-fiber, use useLoader(DRACOLoader, url) or GLTFLoader with a Draco decoder path set via setDecoderPath(). Replace the local 'models/draco/bunny.drc' path with a URL to your own Draco-compressed asset hosted on a CDN or in /public; also set dracoLoader.setDecoderPath() to a CDN path such as 'https://www.gstatic.com/draco/versioned/decoders/1.5.6/' so the WASM decoder is available.
constraints: Draco decoding requires WASM support, available in all modern browsers but adds ~200ms decoder init overhead; not suitable for environments blocking WASM. Draco compression is most beneficial for meshes over ~50k triangles. Shadows and SpotLight increase GPU load; disable shadowMap on low-end mobile. WebGL renderer is required; no WebGPU fallback here.
antiPatterns: Forgetting to call dracoLoader.dispose() after loading causes a WASM memory leak. Not setting setDecoderPath() causes a silent 404 for the decoder scripts. Hardcoding window.innerWidth/innerHeight breaks in contained div layouts — use container.clientWidth/clientHeight instead. Omitting computeVertexNormals() on loaded geometry results in flat, faceted shading.
accessibilityNotes: Wrap the canvas in a region with aria-label describing the 3D object (e.g. 'Interactive 3D product view'). Provide a static fallback image for users with reduced-motion preferences by checking prefers-reduced-motion and stopping the animation loop (cancel setAnimationLoop). The orbiting camera is passive and non-interactive so no keyboard controls are needed, but consider pausing animation when the element is off-screen using IntersectionObserver.

technique: animated FBX character model viewer with skeleton, morph targets, and switchable animation clips
description: Displays a fully rigged and animated 3D character or object model loaded from an FBX file, playing skeletal animations on a ground-plane stage with fog and directional shadow lighting. Suits product showcases, game character previews, virtual try-on pages, or interactive portfolio sections featuring 3D assets.
usageNote: In React or Next.js, initialize the renderer, scene, and FBXLoader inside a useEffect with a canvas ref, storing the animation frame ID for cleanup. Use react-three-fiber with @react-three/drei's useFBX hook as a cleaner alternative. Replace all 'models/fbx/' paths with your own hosted asset URLs (CDN, /public folder, or presigned S3 URLs); FBX files must be accessible via HTTP, not imported as modules. Dispose mixer, geometries, materials, and textures in the useEffect cleanup function.
constraints: FBX parsing is CPU-heavy and can cause noticeable frame drops on low-end mobile hardware, especially with large skeletal meshes or embedded textures. Requires WebGL renderer with shadowMap support. File sizes for FBX assets can be large (multi-MB), so consider converting to glTF/GLB for production use. Not suitable for scenes needing more than one or two simultaneous animated characters without instancing optimizations.
antiPatterns: Forgetting to dispose skeleton, geometry, materials, and textures when swapping models causes GPU memory leaks. Hardcoding window.innerWidth/innerHeight instead of using the container's bounding rect breaks embedded (non-fullscreen) layouts. Not cancelling the animation loop or disconnecting the Timer on unmount causes errors in React strict mode. Ignoring scale normalization leads to models appearing invisible or filling the entire view.
accessibilityNotes: Wrap the canvas in a region with aria-label describing the 3D content. Provide a static screenshot or image fallback for users with prefers-reduced-motion or those on devices where WebGL is unavailable. Keyboard users cannot interact with OrbitControls by default; add keyboard pan/rotate handlers or expose camera position controls via accessible UI. Screen readers receive no meaningful content from the canvas; use visually-hidden descriptive text alongside it.

technique: interactive 3D NURBS model viewer with orbit controls
description: Renders a smooth NURBS-based 3D model loaded from an FBX file, displayed on a dark grid floor with full 360° orbit interaction. Suits product configurators, industrial design showcases, CAD visualization portals, or any site needing precise smooth-surface 3D model presentation.
usageNote: In React/Next.js, move all init logic into a useEffect with a canvas ref, assign the renderer to the ref element instead of appending to body, and return a cleanup function that calls renderer.dispose() and removes event listeners. Replace the local 'models/fbx/nurbs.fbx' path with a URL pointing to your own hosted FBX asset (CDN, public folder, or API route). With react-three-fiber, use the useLoader hook with FBXLoader and place the result in a primitive component.
constraints: Requires WebGL support; not suitable for WebGL-unsupported environments. FBX with NURBS geometry can be heavy — ensure the model is optimized before production use. Mobile performance depends heavily on model polygon count; NURBS tessellation may spike CPU on load. OrbitControls require pointer events so touch is supported but may feel heavy on low-end phones.
antiPatterns: Forgetting to dispose the FBXLoader result (geometry, materials, textures) on component unmount causes memory leaks. Hardcoding window.innerWidth/window.innerHeight breaks in contained layouts — use the parent container's dimensions instead. Not handling the async load callback means the scene may render before the model appears with no error feedback. Skipping controls.update() after setting the target breaks the initial camera orientation.
accessibilityNotes: Provide a static hero image fallback for users with prefers-reduced-motion or no WebGL. Add an aria-label on the canvas element describing the model content. Keyboard navigation is not natively supported by OrbitControls — consider adding custom keyboard handlers for rotation/zoom. Screen readers receive no semantic information from the canvas; supplement with descriptive surrounding text.

technique: 3D GCode toolpath visualizer with orbit controls and asset switcher
description: Renders the layered extrusion paths of a 3D print file as colored line geometry in a dark 3D space, allowing users to orbit and inspect the toolpath from any angle. Suits maker/fabrication platforms, 3D printing services, or CAD/CAM web apps that need to preview print files before submission.
usageNote: Wrap the init logic in a useEffect with a canvas ref; assign renderer.domElement to the ref instead of appending to document.body. Dispose the renderer on cleanup. Replace 'models/gcode/' paths with your own hosted .gcode files — serve them from /public in Next.js or an accessible CDN URL. Pass the URL directly to loader.load(). For react-three-fiber, use a <lineSegments> primitive after parsing, though the GCodeLoader is easier to use in vanilla Three.js via useEffect.
constraints: GCode files with many thousands of lines can produce very dense line geometry and stress the GPU; test with real files before production. Requires WebGL renderer — no fallback to WebGPU or CSS. Mobile support is functional but orbit controls are finger-driven and the line geometry can be demanding on low-end mobile GPUs. Not suitable for real-time animation-heavy pages.
antiPatterns: Forgetting to traverse and dispose both geometry and material when swapping assets causes memory leaks. Hardcoding window.innerWidth/innerHeight instead of measuring the container breaks embedded layouts. Omitting the resize handler causes distorted perspective on viewport changes. Using large GCode files without LOD or streaming will stall the main thread during parsing.
accessibilityNotes: The visualization is purely decorative/functional for sighted users; provide a text summary of the loaded model (name, estimated dimensions) for screen readers via an aria-live region. Add a reduced-motion check to skip auto-spin or any animation loop. Supply a static PNG preview image as a fallback for environments without WebGL support.

technique: interactive 3D GLTF model viewer with HDR environment lighting and animated camera orbit
description: A photorealistic 3D model displayed against a blurred HDR panoramic background with ACES filmic tone mapping, supporting built-in animations and smooth orbit controls. Ideal for product pages, portfolios, digital showrooms, or any site needing an interactive 3D asset showcase.
usageNote: Wrap initialization in a useEffect with a canvas ref in React/Next.js; assign renderer.domElement to the ref instead of appending to document.body. Use react-three-fiber's <Canvas> with <Environment files=...> and <useGLTF> hooks as a cleaner alternative. Replace the UltraHDRLoader texture path with a bundler-imported HDR file (e.g., import hdr from './royal_esplanade_2k.hdr.jpg' with a file-loader, or serve from /public in Next.js). Replace the Khronos GitHub URLs with your own hosted .glb files or a CDN URL.
constraints: High performance cost due to HDR environment loading, shader compilation, and potentially complex GLTF meshes; compileAsync mitigates frame hitches on model swap. Requires WebGL with floating-point texture support for HDR. Not ideal for low-end mobile devices or pages needing fast initial load; consider a static image fallback below a performance threshold. Best suited for feature sections, not repeated components.
antiPatterns: Forgetting to call renderer.dispose(), geometry.dispose(), and material.dispose() when the component unmounts or the model changes — especially critical since models are swapped dynamically. Hardcoding window.innerWidth/window.innerHeight instead of measuring the container element. Not cancelling in-flight loads when a new model is requested (the loadId guard pattern here is correct — preserve it). Forgetting to remove the resize event listener on unmount.
accessibilityNotes: The 3D canvas is not screen-reader accessible; add an aria-label describing the displayed model and a visually-hidden text description. Respect prefers-reduced-motion by pausing AnimationMixer playback and disabling OrbitControls auto-rotate when the media query matches. Provide a static rendered image fallback for users with WebGL disabled or on very low-end devices. Ensure any GUI controls (model selector) are also exposed as accessible HTML controls outside the canvas.

technique: keyframe-animated GLTF model viewer with orbit controls and PMREM environment lighting
description: A 3D animated product or character model plays a looping keyframe animation inside a softly lit room environment, with smooth orbit controls allowing full 360-degree inspection. Ideal for product showcase sections, interactive hero banners, or digital twin presentations on e-commerce, portfolio, or marketing sites.
usageNote: In React/Next.js, wrap all renderer, scene, camera, and loader setup inside a useEffect with a canvas ref (not document.getElementById). Return a cleanup function that calls renderer.dispose(), mixer teardown, and renderer.setAnimationLoop(null). Replace the hardcoded cloud asset URL with your own hosted GLTF/GLB URL (a CDN path, public folder path, or environment variable). For react-three-fiber, use useGLTF from @react-three/drei and useFrame for the mixer update. KTX2Loader needs the renderer reference, so initialize it after renderer creation inside the effect.
constraints: Requires WebGL (not WebGPU). DRACO and KTX2 decoding add ~500KB WASM overhead; use only if the GLTF actually uses those compressions. Animated GLTF models with Draco geometry and KTX2 textures are moderately GPU-intensive; test on mid-range mobile. RoomEnvironment PMREM generation costs a one-time GPU bake on load. Not suitable for very low-end or legacy mobile WebGL1-only devices.
antiPatterns: Forgetting to call renderer.dispose() and mixer teardown on component unmount causing memory leaks in SPAs. Hardcoding window.innerWidth/window.innerHeight instead of using a ResizeObserver on the container element. Not awaiting DRACOLoader and KTX2Loader decoder paths before loading the GLTF, leading to silent decode errors. Re-creating the PMREMGenerator on every render. Leaving the animation loop running after the component unmounts.
accessibilityNotes: Respect prefers-reduced-motion by pausing or stopping the AnimationMixer and disabling auto-rotate when the media query matches. Provide a static fallback image (og:image or a <noscript> img) for screen readers and crawlers. Add an aria-label to the canvas element describing the model content. Ensure keyboard users can interact via tab-focusable UI controls rather than relying solely on mouse orbit.

technique: physically-based GLTF model viewer with anisotropic texture filtering and HDR environment lighting
description: A high-fidelity 3D product or object viewer with realistic anisotropic surface shading and an HDR environment map providing accurate reflections and lighting. Ideal for product detail pages, luxury brand showcases, e-commerce 3D viewers, or portfolio sections where material quality is paramount.
usageNote: In React or Next.js, wrap initialization in a useEffect with a canvas ref and return a cleanup function that calls renderer.dispose(). Replace the hdrLoader path with your own hosted UltraHDR .hdr.jpg file and the gltfLoader path with your own .glb model URL (e.g. from a CDN or /public folder). With react-three-fiber, use useLoader(GLTFLoader, url) and useLoader(UltraHDRLoader, url) inside a Canvas component, and set gl.toneMapping and gl.toneMappingExposure on the renderer via the gl prop.
constraints: Requires WebGL with anisotropic filtering extension support (virtually universal on desktop, broadly supported on mobile). Loading a UltraHDR environment and a GLB simultaneously may cause noticeable load time on slow connections; use compressed textures and Draco-compressed GLB where possible. Not suitable for low-powered or very old mobile GPUs due to HDR environment cost.
antiPatterns: Forgetting to dispose the HDR texture and GLTF scene on component unmount causing memory leaks; hardcoding window.innerWidth/innerHeight instead of using a container element's dimensions; omitting the resize listener or not updating camera.aspect on resize; not setting texture.mapping to EquirectangularReflectionMapping before assigning to scene.environment; forgetting to call controls.update() after programmatic target changes.
accessibilityNotes: Provide a static high-quality product image fallback for users with prefers-reduced-motion or when WebGL is unavailable. Add an aria-label to the canvas element describing the 3D model. Orbit controls are mouse/touch driven with no keyboard support by default; consider adding keyboard-driven rotation for accessibility. Screen readers will not interpret the 3D scene, so supplementary descriptive text should accompany the viewer.

technique: interactive 3D GLTF model viewer with AVIF texture compression and orbit controls
description: Renders a fully textured 3D architectural or environment model (forest house) with AVIF-compressed textures and Draco geometry compression, supporting smooth mouse-driven orbit navigation. Ideal for product configurators, real estate previews, portfolio showcases, or any site section requiring a high-fidelity interactive 3D scene with optimized asset delivery.
usageNote: Wrap the init and render logic inside a useEffect hook with a canvas ref in React/Next.js; pass the ref's current element to the WebGLRenderer constructor instead of appending to document.body. For react-three-fiber, use useGLTF from @react-three/drei which handles GLTFLoader and DRACOLoader internally. Replace the hardcoded 'models/gltf/AVIFTest/' path with your own CDN or /public asset path; ensure your server serves .glb and .avif with correct MIME types. Set the DRACOLoader decoder path to a CDN such as 'https://www.gstatic.com/draco/versioned/decoders/1.5.6/' if not bundling locally.
constraints: Requires WebGL1 or WebGL2 capable GPU; AVIF texture support depends on browser (Chrome 85+, Firefox 93+, Safari 16+ with caveats). Draco decompression adds a WASM download cost (~200KB) on first load. Large GLTF scenes with high-resolution AVIF textures may exceed mobile GPU memory budgets; test on mid-range Android devices. Not suitable for IE11 or very low-end WebGL contexts.
antiPatterns: Forgetting to call renderer.dispose() and controls.dispose() on component unmount causes GPU memory leaks in React SPAs. Not removing the resize event listener on cleanup. Hardcoding window.innerWidth/window.innerHeight instead of measuring the parent container breaks embedded/non-fullscreen layouts. Omitting antialias on high-DPI screens produces jagged edges. Failing to set the correct DRACO decoder path results in a silent load failure with no model displayed.
accessibilityNotes: The 3D canvas is not keyboard navigable by default; add tabIndex and keydown handlers to move the orbit target for keyboard users. Provide a static screenshot fallback image via a <noscript> tag or a CSS background for users with JS disabled or prefers-reduced-motion set. Add an aria-label to the canvas element describing the scene content. Consider a 2D image carousel as a reduced-motion alternative since the model only animates on user interaction.

technique: compressed GLTF 3D model viewer with orbit controls and PBR environment lighting
description: A photorealistic 3D product model rendered with ACES filmic tone mapping and environment-based PBR lighting, displayed on a subtle grid floor with full 360-degree orbit camera control. Ideal for e-commerce product pages, interactive product configurators, or brand showcase sections where users can inspect a 3D object from any angle.
usageNote: Wrap initialization in a useEffect with a canvas ref in React/Next.js, passing the ref to WebGLRenderer instead of creating a div. Use react-three-fiber alternatively with <Canvas> and useLoader(GLTFLoader, url). Replace 'models/gltf/coffeemat.glb' with a publicly hosted or CDN-served .glb URL that was pre-processed with gltfpack using -cc and -tc flags to retain KTX2 and meshopt compression; ensure the KTX2Loader's detectSupport receives the renderer instance before loading.
constraints: Requires WebGL2 for KTX2/BasisLZ texture decompression; meshopt compression reduces geometry transfer size but needs the MeshoptDecoder WASM module to be available. Moderate GPU cost due to PBR environment maps and ACES tone mapping. Mobile supported but may be slow on low-end devices with complex models. Not suitable for rendering many simultaneous compressed models without memory management.
antiPatterns: Forgetting to call ktx2Loader.dispose() and pmremGenerator.dispose() after use leaks GPU memory. Hardcoding window.innerWidth/innerHeight instead of using a container ref breaks layout in component-based frameworks. Not setting the KTX2Loader basis transcoder path (setTranscoderPath) can silently fail on some browsers. Using an unprocessed GLTF without meshopt/KTX2 compression while keeping the specialized loaders causes silent no-ops.
accessibilityNotes: Provide a static high-quality product image as a fallback for users with prefers-reduced-motion or on devices where WebGL is unavailable. Add an aria-label to the canvas element describing the product. Orbit controls are mouse/touch driven with no keyboard equivalents by default; add keyboard event listeners or use OrbitControls' built-in keyboard support and document it for screen reader users. Include a visible text description of the product alongside the 3D viewer.

technique: chromatic dispersion glass material on 3D model with IBL environment
description: A high-fidelity 3D glass or crystal object rendered with chromatic dispersion — light splitting into rainbow-like spectral colors as it refracts through the material — set against a softly blurred room-environment background. Ideal for luxury product showcases, jewelry, perfume bottles, gemstone displays, or premium landing pages where tactile material quality needs to be communicated.
usageNote: In React/Next.js, wrap the init logic in a useEffect with a canvas ref, assign renderer.domElement to the ref's container, and clean up renderer and controls on unmount. Replace the local 'models/gltf/DispersionTest.glb' path with your own hosted GLTF/GLB URL (CDN, public folder, or API route). In react-three-fiber, use @react-three/drei's useGLTF hook and Environment preset instead of manual loader and RoomEnvironment.
constraints: Requires WebGL with support for transmission/dispersion extensions (WebGL 2 preferred); dispersion is a physically-based material feature that may not render correctly on all mobile GPUs or older browsers. Performance cost is moderate-to-high due to PMREM generation and transmission rendering passes. Not suitable for scenes requiring many simultaneous transparent objects.
antiPatterns: Forgetting to dispose the PMREMGenerator and RoomEnvironment after baking the env texture causes GPU memory leaks. Hardcoding window.innerWidth/innerHeight instead of using a container ref breaks layout in component-based apps. Not removing the resize event listener on unmount causes stale closures. Skipping antialias on the renderer noticeably degrades glass edge quality.
accessibilityNotes: Provide a high-quality static product image as a fallback for users with prefers-reduced-motion or on devices where WebGL is unavailable. The 3D canvas is purely decorative; add aria-hidden='true' to the container and ensure surrounding product information is accessible via standard HTML. Orbit controls are mouse/touch driven — add a visible label or tooltip explaining drag-to-rotate for discoverability.

technique: GPU-instanced 3D model display with HDR environment lighting and orbit controls
description: Renders multiple instances of a detailed PBR 3D model lit by a high-dynamic-range equirectangular environment map, producing photorealistic reflections and lighting. Ideal for product showcase pages, 3D asset galleries, or technology/gaming brand hero sections where multiple identical objects (e.g., a product array) are displayed efficiently.
usageNote: Wrap the init/render logic inside a React useEffect with a canvas ref, returning a cleanup function that calls renderer.dispose() and removes the event listener. Replace the UltraHDRLoader path with a CDN or /public folder URL for the HDR image, and host the GLTF and its assets on a CDN or in /public, passing the full URL to loader.load(). In react-three-fiber, use <primitive object={gltf.scene}> after loading with useGLTF, and set environment via <Environment> from @react-three/drei.
constraints: GPU instancing requires WebGL2 for best performance; broadly supported on modern desktop and mobile GPUs. UltraHDR texture loading is bandwidth-heavy — use compressed or lower-resolution HDR alternatives for mobile. High instance counts and complex PBR materials can be demanding; test on mid-range mobile devices. Not suited for WebGL1-only fallback environments.
antiPatterns: Forgetting to dispose the renderer, geometry, materials, and textures on component unmount causing memory leaks. Not handling the async HDR + GLTF load sequence, leading to renders before assets are ready. Hardcoding window.innerWidth/innerHeight instead of using a container ref for embedded canvas sizing. Omitting toneMapping settings resulting in washed-out or overly dark PBR materials.
accessibilityNotes: Provide a static fallback image of the 3D scene for users with prefers-reduced-motion enabled or when WebGL is unavailable. Add an aria-label to the canvas element describing the 3D content. Orbit controls are mouse/touch driven with no keyboard equivalent by default — add keyboard-driven camera controls or a skip link for screen reader users. Ensure surrounding page content remains navigable without the 3D view.

technique: iridescent 3D model viewer with HDR environment lighting and auto-rotate
description: A richly lit 3D object with iridescent (rainbow/oil-slick) surface shading rotates slowly against a photorealistic HDR environment backdrop. Ideal for product showcase sections on e-commerce sites, luxury brand landing pages, or portfolio hero sections where a physical object needs to feel premium and tactile.
usageNote: In React/Next.js, wrap the renderer setup in a useEffect with a canvas ref (or use react-three-fiber with <mesh> and MeshPhysicalMaterial iridescence props). Replace 'textures/equirectangular/venice_sunset_1k.hdr' with a CDN-hosted HDR file (e.g. from polyhaven.com) and 'models/gltf/IridescenceLamp.glb' with your own product GLB hosted on your CDN or public folder. Clean up renderer, controls, and event listeners in the useEffect return function.
constraints: Requires WebGL2 for full physical material iridescence support; not suitable for very low-end or old mobile GPUs. HDR environment loading adds network overhead (~1–3 MB). The ACESFilmic tone mapping and iridescence shading are moderately GPU-intensive; test frame rate on mid-range mobile. Not ideal for pages requiring instant interactivity above the fold without a loading state.
antiPatterns: Forgetting to call renderer.dispose() and controls.dispose() on unmount causing memory leaks; not handling the async load failure gracefully (blank scene with no error UI); hardcoding window.innerWidth/innerHeight instead of using the parent container's dimensions; omitting the resize event listener cleanup; loading the HDR from a local path that doesn't exist in production.
accessibilityNotes: Add a prefers-reduced-motion media query check to disable controls.autoRotate and the animation loop, replacing with a static rendered frame. Provide a high-quality fallback image (e.g. <noscript> or CSS background) for users without WebGL support. The canvas should have aria-label describing the object (e.g. 'Interactive 3D product view') and role='img' so screen readers announce it meaningfully.

technique: progressive GLTF loading with HDR environment, multi-model animated scene, and atmospheric fog
description: A dark, atmospheric 3D scene featuring multiple animated GLTF models (environment, airship, product) that stream in progressively with HDR image-based lighting and depth fog, creating a cinematic product or world showcase. Ideal for hero sections of product launch pages, game landing pages, interactive 3D storefronts, or immersive brand experiences where assets load incrementally rather than blocking the user.
usageNote: Wrap all init and animate logic inside a useEffect hook with a ref-attached canvas (renderer.domElement appended to a ref div). Return a cleanup function that calls renderer.dispose(), controls.dispose(), and cancels the animation frame. Replace the HDRLoader path with assets served from your /public folder (e.g. '/textures/equirectangular/quarry_01_1k.hdr'). The @needle-tools/gltf-progressive package must be installed via npm. In react-three-fiber, use useGLTF with Suspense boundaries per model and @react-three/drei's Environment component for HDR.
constraints: High GPU cost due to HDR environment, tone mapping, fog, multiple GLTF scenes, and continuous animation mixer updates — not suitable for low-end mobile devices. Requires WebGL2-capable hardware. Progressive loading via @needle-tools/gltf-progressive is a third-party dependency not included in the three.js core and must be explicitly installed. External CDN model URLs (cloud.needle.tools) must remain accessible or be replaced with self-hosted assets.
antiPatterns: Forgetting to cancel the requestAnimationFrame loop and dispose renderer/controls on component unmount, causing memory leaks in SPA routing. Hardcoding window.innerWidth/window.innerHeight instead of measuring the container element, breaking layout in non-fullscreen contexts. Not handling load errors for the three external GLTF URLs. Skipping AnimationMixer cleanup (mixer.stopAllAction, mixer.uncacheRoot) when models are removed. Failing to replace local texture paths before deployment.
accessibilityNotes: Provide a static fallback image (e.g. a rendered screenshot as a poster element) for users with prefers-reduced-motion or low-power devices. Add an aria-label or visually-hidden text description of the scene for screen readers. Pause the animation loop and mixer when the document is hidden (use the Timer's connect method or a visibilitychange listener). Keyboard navigation is not applicable to the canvas, so ensure surrounding page content remains fully accessible.

technique: 3D fabric/textile product viewer with sheen material rendering and orbit controls
description: A photorealistic 3D upholstered chair rendered with physically-based sheen material simulating velvet or fabric micro-fiber light scattering, set against a neutral studio environment. Ideal for e-commerce product pages, furniture configurators, or luxury brand showcases where tactile material quality needs to be communicated visually.
usageNote: Wrap the init and animate logic inside a useEffect hook with a canvas ref in React/Next.js, appending the renderer domElement to the ref instead of document.body. Replace the local 'models/gltf/SheenChair.glb' path with a URL pointing to your own CDN-hosted or public-folder GLB file (e.g. '/models/SheenChair.glb' in Next.js public dir). Remove the lil-gui debug panel for production; expose sheen as a React state prop instead. Use react-three-fiber for a more idiomatic React integration with R3F's useGLTF hook.
constraints: Requires WebGL 2.0 for full PBR sheen support; falls back gracefully on WebGL 1.0 but sheen may not render correctly. Moderate GPU cost due to PMREM environment generation and ACESFilmic tone mapping. Mobile performance is acceptable for mid-range devices but PMREM generation should be done once at startup. Not suitable for low-end or older mobile hardware without LOD reduction.
antiPatterns: Forgetting to call pmremGenerator.dispose() after generating the environment texture causes a GPU memory leak. Not cleaning up the renderer, controls, and animation loop on component unmount in React leads to memory leaks and ghost render loops. Hardcoding window.innerWidth/innerHeight instead of using the container element's dimensions breaks embedded or partial-page viewers. Leaving the debug GUI visible in production exposes internal material parameters.
accessibilityNotes: Provide a high-quality static product image fallback for users with prefers-reduced-motion enabled or when WebGL is unavailable. The 3D canvas has no inherent keyboard navigation; add aria-label to the canvas element describing the product and ensure all product details are also available as standard HTML text. OrbitControls are mouse/touch-only by default; add keyboard controls or a visible 'rotate' affordance for accessibility.

technique: auto-rotating 3D product viewer with glass transmission and HDR environment lighting
description: A richly lit, slowly rotating 3D object with physically-based glass/transmission materials (translucent, refractive surfaces) set against a blurred HDR equirectangular panorama background. Ideal for premium product showcases, e-commerce hero sections, or luxury brand landing pages where tactile material quality needs to be communicated.
usageNote: Wrap all init logic inside a useEffect with a canvas ref in React/Next.js; pass the ref's current element to the WebGLRenderer instead of appending to document.body. Replace UltraHDRLoader path with a CDN-hosted or /public-folder .hdr.jpg and the GLTFLoader path with your own .glb hosted in /public or a CDN. In react-three-fiber, use <Environment> from @react-three/drei for the HDR and <useGLTF> for model loading. Clean up renderer, controls, and animation loop in the useEffect return.
constraints: Transmission materials require WebGL2 and have significant GPU cost because they trigger an extra render pass; avoid on low-end mobile or scenes with many transparent objects. The UltraHDR texture is large — lazy-load it or show a placeholder while it fetches. Not suitable for WebGL1 fallback targets.
antiPatterns: Forgetting to dispose the renderer, geometry, textures, and AnimationMixer on component unmount causing memory leaks; not calling controls.update() inside the animation loop when autoRotate is enabled; hardcoding window.innerWidth/innerHeight instead of measuring the container element; omitting the DRACOLoader decoder path which silently breaks compressed model loading.
accessibilityNotes: Pause or freeze autoRotate when prefers-reduced-motion is detected (query via window.matchMedia). Provide a static high-quality product image as a <noscript> or CSS background fallback. Add an aria-label to the canvas element describing the product. Ensure surrounding page content (name, price, description) is accessible to screen readers independently of the 3D view.

technique: 3D product viewer with real-time material/color variant switching
description: A photorealistic 3D product model rendered under HDR environment lighting with smooth orbit controls, allowing users to switch between named material variants (e.g. colorways or finish options) in real time without reloading the model. Ideal for e-commerce product pages, configurators, or brand showcases where customers need to preview item variants interactively.
usageNote: Wrap the init logic inside a useEffect with a canvas ref in React/Next.js, attaching the renderer to the ref element instead of appending to document.body. Use react-three-fiber's useGLTF hook for cleaner GLTF loading. Replace local asset paths (textures/equirectangular/ and models/gltf/) with CDN-hosted or public/ folder URLs for the HDR environment map and GLTF model. Expose variant selection as React state bound to a UI dropdown or swatch component instead of lil-gui.
constraints: Requires WebGL with reasonably modern GPU for HDR tone mapping and high-quality material rendering. GLTF model must use the KHR_materials_variants extension for variant switching to work. HDR environment texture adds significant download weight (~2–8 MB); use compressed KTX2 alternatives for mobile. Not suitable for very low-end or older mobile devices due to environment mapping cost.
antiPatterns: Forgetting to dispose of old materials when variants are switched, causing GPU memory leaks over time. Not cleaning up the renderer, controls, and GUI on component unmount in React. Hardcoding window.innerWidth/window.innerHeight instead of measuring the container element. Assuming the GLTF file has KHR_materials_variants without graceful fallback. Forgetting to call render() after async material swaps complete.
accessibilityNotes: The 3D viewer has no keyboard navigation by default; add keyboard shortcuts or ARIA-labeled buttons for variant selection. Provide static product images as fallbacks for users with prefers-reduced-motion or when WebGL is unavailable. The orbit controls are mouse/touch-only; consider adding labelled camera preset buttons. Screen readers cannot perceive the 3D scene, so mirror variant selection state in visible text or visually hidden ARIA live regions.

technique: IFC building model viewer with merged geometry and orbit controls
description: Renders a full architectural building model loaded from an IFC file as a 3D scene with opaque and transparent surfaces, directional lighting, and interactive orbit navigation. Ideal for architecture firm portfolios, construction project dashboards, BIM (Building Information Modeling) viewers, real estate platforms, or facility management tools that need to display complex building geometry in the browser.
usageNote: Wrap the init function inside a React useEffect with a canvas ref, passing the ref's current element to the WebGLRenderer instead of appending to document.body. Install the 'web-ifc' npm package and host its WASM binary either via the CDN path already used or copy it into your public folder and update WEB_IFC_WASM_PATH. Replace the local fetch path 'models/ifc/rac_advanced_sample_project.ifc' with a URL to your own IFC file served from your public directory or a remote CDN. In Next.js, use dynamic import with ssr: false because web-ifc uses WebAssembly which is browser-only.
constraints: High performance cost: IFC models can contain hundreds of thousands of faces; geometry merging helps but mobile GPU memory limits may cause crashes on large models. Requires WebGL 1 or 2; no fallback for WebGL-unsupported browsers. WASM loading adds cold-start latency. Not suitable for embedding as a decorative background element; best used as a dedicated full-page or panel viewer.
antiPatterns: Forgetting to call ifcAPI.CloseModel() and geometry.delete() causing WASM heap leaks. Not disposing merged BufferGeometry and materials on component unmount in React. Hardcoding window.innerWidth/innerHeight instead of using the container element's dimensions. Blocking the main thread during large model parsing without a loading indicator. Omitting the resize event listener or failing to update camera.aspect on resize.
accessibilityNotes: Provide a static screenshot or rendered image fallback for users who cannot interact with 3D content or have WebGL disabled. Add an aria-label to the canvas element describing the building model. Expose keyboard controls or UI buttons for zoom/pan/rotate as an alternative to mouse-only OrbitControls. For reduced-motion preferences, disable auto-rotation and keep the model static on load.

technique: async image bitmap texture loading onto rotating 3D cubes
description: Multiple textured 3D cubes spawn asynchronously on a grid, rotating as a group in 3D space. Suits product showcases, interactive loading demos, or portfolio sections that need to visualize progressive asset loading or multi-texture 3D objects.
usageNote: Wrap the init logic inside a useEffect with a canvas ref in React/Next.js; assign the renderer to the ref's current element instead of appending to document.body. Replace local texture paths (textures/planets/earth_atmos_2048.jpg) with paths inside your /public folder or CDN URLs. Use ImageBitmapLoader for performance-sensitive paths and dispose ImageBitmap after GPU upload as shown. For react-three-fiber, replace ImageBitmapLoader with useLoader(THREE.ImageBitmapLoader, url) and apply the resulting CanvasTexture to a meshBasicMaterial.
constraints: Requires WebGL renderer; ImageBitmapLoader is not supported in all older browsers (no IE11). GPU texture memory grows with each cube added—limit dynamically spawned cubes for mobile. CanvasTexture from ImageBitmap is more memory-efficient than ImageLoader on supported browsers. Not suited for environments where OffscreenCanvas/ImageBitmap are unavailable (some Safari versions pre-15).
antiPatterns: Forgetting to call texture.source.data.close() on ImageBitmap after GPU upload causes memory leaks. Not disposing old textures and materials when cubes are removed will exhaust GPU memory. Hardcoding window.innerWidth/window.innerHeight instead of using a container element size breaks embedded canvas layouts. Omitting the resize event listener causes distorted aspect ratio on viewport changes. Reusing the same geometry instance across materials is fine here but forgetting to dispose it on unmount leaks GPU buffers.
accessibilityNotes: The animation loop runs continuously; add a prefers-reduced-motion media query check to pause or skip rotation for users with vestibular sensitivities. Provide a static fallback image of the textured cube for screen readers via an aria-label on the canvas element. No keyboard interaction is implemented; if interaction is added, ensure focus management and keyboard controls are included.

technique: KMZ/KML 3D model viewer with orbit controls
description: Renders a KMZ (zipped KML/Collada) 3D model on a grid plane with directional lighting and full 360-degree orbit camera control. Suits product configurators, geospatial asset viewers, architecture previews, or any site that needs to display Google Earth-compatible 3D assets interactively.
usageNote: In React or Next.js, wrap the entire init block in a useEffect with a canvas ref, passing the ref's current element to the WebGLRenderer constructor instead of appending to document.body. Use react-three-fiber's useLoader or a useEffect-based loader to fetch the KMZ file. Replace the hardcoded './models/kmz/Box.kmz' path with a URL pointing to your own asset hosted on a CDN or served from your public/ folder (e.g. '/models/Box.kmz' in Next.js). Return a cleanup function from useEffect that calls renderer.dispose() and removes the event listeners.
constraints: Requires WebGL support; KMZLoader parses zipped KML/Collada files which may include embedded textures, so large files can cause slow initial load. Not suited for very low-end mobile devices due to geometry and texture decoding overhead. Only renders on-demand (no animation loop), so CPU/GPU usage is low at rest.
antiPatterns: Forgetting to dispose the renderer and remove the resize listener on component unmount, causing memory leaks in SPAs. Hardcoding window.innerWidth/window.innerHeight instead of measuring the container element, breaking layouts where the canvas is not full-screen. Not handling loader errors, leaving a blank canvas if the KMZ URL is wrong or CORS-blocked.
accessibilityNotes: The 3D canvas has no keyboard navigation or screen reader description by default; add an aria-label to the canvas element describing the model, and provide a static fallback image for users who cannot use 3D. Orbit controls are mouse/touch-only; consider adding keyboard arrow-key handlers for accessibility. No animation loop means prefers-reduced-motion is effectively respected, but confirm no auto-rotation is added later.

technique: interactive LEGO/LDraw brick model viewer with step-by-step build animation and orbit controls
description: Renders fully detailed LEGO-style brick models parsed from LDraw (.ldr/.mpd) files with proper part edges, conditional lines, smooth normals, and step-by-step build progression in a lit room environment. Ideal for toy product pages, educational assembly guides, collectible showcases, or any site needing interactive 3D brick model display.
usageNote: Wrap in a React useEffect with a canvas ref: create the renderer targeting the ref element, instantiate OrbitControls and LDrawLoader inside the effect, and return a cleanup function that disposes renderer and cancels the animation loop. Replace all local 'models/ldraw/' and 'models/*.mpd' paths with URLs pointing to your CDN or API route that serves pre-packed .mpd files and the LDraw parts library; the parts library path is set via lDrawLoader.setPath().
