Requires WebGL2-capable renderer. LDraw parts library files must be accessible at runtime (cannot be statically bundled without packing). Model merging (LDrawUtils.mergeModel) can help performance but removes per-step build animation.
antiPatterns: Forgetting to dispose the LDrawLoader-generated geometry and materials when switching models or unmounting the component causes severe memory leaks. Hardcoding window.innerWidth/window.innerHeight instead of using the container element dimensions breaks layout in embedded or partial-page contexts. Not removing the old model from the scene before loading a new one causes duplicate geometry. Skipping the progress bar or load indicator leaves users with a blank canvas during the long parse phase.
accessibilityNotes: Provide a static image fallback (product photo or render) for users with prefers-reduced-motion or no WebGL support. The 3D canvas is not navigable by keyboard or screen reader by default; add an aria-label to the canvas element describing the model and include a text description of the object. Orbit controls have no keyboard bindings by default—add arrow-key handlers or use OrbitControls' built-in keyboard support and document it for users.

technique: animated MD2 skeletal character with morph targets, swappable skins and weapons, orbit camera
description: A fully animated 3D game-style humanoid character stands on a grass ground plane, lit by two spotlights with shadow casting, and can cycle through multiple skins, weapons, and named animations in real time. Suits game portfolio showcases, interactive character selectors, weapon/skin customization previews, or retro-gaming tribute sections.
usageNote: In React/Next.js, initialize the renderer and MD2Character inside a useEffect with a canvas ref, returning a cleanup that calls renderer.dispose() and removes event listeners. Replace all local asset paths (textures/terrain/grasslight-big.jpg, models/md2/ratamahatta/) with URLs served from your /public folder or a CDN; pass them into the config.baseUrl and texture loader accordingly. With react-three-fiber, MD2Character is an imperative helper so keep it in a useEffect or a custom useThree hook rather than as JSX.
constraints: Requires WebGL renderer with shadow maps enabled; high draw call and texture count due to multiple weapon meshes. MD2 morph-target animation is CPU-assisted and moderately expensive; avoid running more than one or two characters simultaneously on mobile. Not suitable for WebGPU renderer without porting the MD2Character loader. Requires network fetching of many small MD2 and PNG assets, so cold-load time can be significant.
antiPatterns: Forgetting to call renderer.dispose() and character mesh geometry/material dispose on unmount; not cancelling the animation loop (setAnimationLoop(null)) on cleanup; hardcoding window.innerWidth/innerHeight instead of measuring a container element; neglecting to call camera.updateProjectionMatrix() on resize; loading all weapon meshes eagerly when only one is shown.
accessibilityNotes: Provide a static screenshot or poster image as a fallback for users with prefers-reduced-motion or no WebGL support. The 3D canvas is purely decorative; wrap it in an aria-hidden container and provide adjacent text describing the character if it conveys meaningful content. GUI controls (lil-gui) are not keyboard-accessible by default; replace or augment them with native HTML controls for weapon/skin/animation switching in production.

technique: animated 3D character showcase with keyboard movement controls and skin variants
description: A grass-terrain environment displaying a row of animated humanoid characters, each wearing a different skin/costume, walking, idling, jumping, or attacking in sync with keyboard input. Suits game landing pages, character selection screens, portfolio showcases, or interactive product configurators that need to display multiple variants of a 3D model side by side.
usageNote: Wrap the entire init/animate block inside a useEffect with a canvas ref in React/Next.js; pass the ref's current element to the WebGLRenderer instead of appending to document.body. Clean up with renderer.dispose() and timer.disconnect() in the useEffect return. Replace local asset paths (textures/terrain/grasslight-big.jpg, models/md2/ogro/) with paths served from your public/ folder or a CDN; in Next.js prefix with the basePath or use next/image for the texture fallback. MD2CharacterComplex is an addon class so import it from the three/addons path as shown.
constraints: High GPU cost: each character shares geometry via shareParts() but still issues multiple draw calls per frame; a full grid of 13+ characters with shadows enabled will stress mobile GPUs. Requires WebGL (not WebGPU). Shadow maps (PCFShadowMap) add additional fill-pass cost. Not suitable for low-end or thermal-throttled mobile devices. MD2 format support is legacy and the asset pipeline is non-trivial to reproduce without the original model files.
antiPatterns: Forgetting to call renderer.dispose() and remove event listeners (keydown/keyup, resize) on component unmount causing memory leaks and ghost input handlers. Hardcoding SCREEN_WIDTH/SCREEN_HEIGHT from window at module scope instead of reading from the canvas ref. Neglecting to call cameraControls.dispose() on teardown. Using window.innerWidth/innerHeight inside a React component instead of the container element's clientWidth/clientHeight, which breaks embedded/non-fullscreen layouts. Not setting renderer.setPixelRatio after resize causes blurry output on retina screens.
accessibilityNotes: Respect prefers-reduced-motion by pausing the animation loop (timer.disconnect() equivalent) and showing a static screenshot fallback when the media query matches. The canvas has no implicit ARIA role; add role='img' and an aria-label describing the character showcase for screen readers. Keyboard controls (WASD/arrow keys) conflict with page scroll; trap focus or add a visible focus ring and instructions. Provide a text description of the character variants for users who cannot see the 3D scene.

technique: MDD morph-target mesh animation with AnimationMixer
description: A 3D mesh deforms continuously through keyframed morph targets loaded from an MDD file, producing fluid shape-shifting animation. Suits product configurators, abstract hero sections, or loading screens needing organic 3D motion without skeletal rigs.
usageNote: Wrap in a useEffect with a canvas ref in React/Next.js; create and return a cleanup function that disposes the renderer, geometry, and mixer. Replace the local 'models/mdd/cube.mdd' path with a URL served from your /public folder or a CDN. In react-three-fiber, use useLoader with a custom MDDLoader integration and useAnimations or a manual useFrame loop calling mixer.update(delta).
constraints: Requires WebGL renderer; MDD files can be large (per-vertex per-frame data), so use only for short clips or low-poly meshes. Mobile GPUs handle morph targets well up to a few dozen targets; beyond that, performance degrades. The MDD format must be pre-converted from DCC tools like Blender.
antiPatterns: Forgetting to call geometry.dispose() and renderer.dispose() on unmount causes GPU memory leaks. Not calling mixer.stopAllAction() before removing the mesh leaves dangling animation state. Hardcoding window.innerWidth/innerHeight instead of using a container ref breaks layouts in apps with fixed sidebars or headers. Neglecting clip.optimize() on long animations wastes memory.
accessibilityNotes: Check prefers-reduced-motion and pause or stop the AnimationMixer if the user has requested reduced motion. Provide a static rendered image fallback via a <noscript> or CSS background for users without WebGL support. The canvas has no semantic meaning; add aria-hidden='true' and place descriptive text nearby for screen readers.

technique: 3D volumetric NRRD medical image viewer with interactive orthogonal slice planes
description: Renders a 3D medical or scientific volumetric dataset as three interactive cross-sectional slice planes (axial, coronal, sagittal) inside a bounding box, with GUI controls to scrub through slices and adjust windowing thresholds. Suited for medical imaging portals, radiology education platforms, scientific data visualization dashboards, or health-tech product demos that need to display 3D scan data in the browser.
usageNote: Wrap the entire init/animate block inside a React useEffect with a canvas ref, passing the ref's current element to the WebGLRenderer constructor instead of appending to document.body. Dispose the renderer and remove event listeners in the useEffect cleanup. Replace 'models/nrrd/I.nrrd' with a URL to your own NRRD file hosted on a CDN or served as a static asset (e.g. in Next.js place it under /public and reference '/your-volume.nrrd'). In react-three-fiber this pattern is harder to map directly; raw three.js with useEffect is recommended. The lil-gui panel should be mounted into a portal or a sibling DOM element, not inside the canvas.
constraints: Requires WebGL 1 or 2; works on modern desktop browsers. NRRD files can be very large (tens to hundreds of MB), making mobile loading impractical due to bandwidth and memory limits. The volumetric slice textures are CPU-computed on load, which can cause a noticeable parse delay for large volumes. Not suitable for real-time or low-powered devices. TrackballControls require pointer events, so touch support is limited.
antiPatterns: Forgetting to call controls.handleResize() and camera.updateProjectionMatrix() on window resize. Not disposing slice textures and geometries when the component unmounts, causing GPU memory leaks. Hardcoding window.innerWidth/innerHeight instead of using the container element's dimensions. Blocking the main thread during NRRD parsing without a loading indicator. Exposing raw volume data URLs without access control on sensitive medical data.
accessibilityNotes: The 3D canvas has no inherent keyboard or screen reader support; provide an ARIA label on the canvas element describing the dataset. Add a static screenshot or description for users who cannot interact with 3D content. The GUI sliders should have visible labels (already present via lil-gui names) but may need focus styles and ARIA attributes for keyboard accessibility. For reduced-motion preferences, the scene is largely static (rotation only on user interaction via TrackballControls), so no animation loop reduction is strictly required, but auto-rotation should not be added.

technique: interactive 3D OBJ/MTL model viewer with orbit controls
description: A textured 3D model loaded from OBJ and MTL files is displayed in an interactive viewer that the user can rotate, zoom, and pan around freely. Ideal for product pages, portfolio showcases, character previews, or any site section that needs a photorealistic or stylized 3D asset presented interactively.
usageNote: In React or Next.js, wrap the setup inside a useEffect hook with a canvas ref passed to the WebGLRenderer instead of appending to document.body. Return a cleanup function that calls renderer.dispose() and removes the resize listener. Replace the local asset paths (models/obj/male02/) with paths to your own OBJ and MTL files hosted in the public directory or via a CDN URL passed to setPath(). With react-three-fiber, use useLoader(OBJLoader, url) combined with useLoader(MTLLoader, url) and apply materials via objLoader.setMaterials().
constraints: Requires WebGL support; OBJ/MTL loading is synchronous-heavy on the main thread for large models, so keep polygon counts reasonable for mobile. Large textures referenced in MTL files can spike memory significantly. Not suitable for extremely low-end or WebGL-disabled devices. OrbitControls add pointer-event overhead on touch screens.
antiPatterns: Forgetting to dispose geometry, materials, and textures when the component unmounts causing memory leaks. Hardcoding window.innerWidth/innerHeight instead of using a container element's dimensions, which breaks embedded layouts. Not calling controls.update() in the animation loop causing damping to malfunction. Omitting materials.preload() before passing to OBJLoader causing texture artifacts.
accessibilityNotes: The canvas has no inherent keyboard or screen reader accessibility. Add an aria-label describing the 3D content and provide a static fallback image for users with prefers-reduced-motion or no WebGL support. Pause the animation loop when the component is not visible using IntersectionObserver to reduce CPU/GPU drain.

technique: interactive 3D point cloud viewer with orbit controls and material GUI
description: Renders a dense cloud of colored or monochrome 3D points forming a scanned real-world object or environment, with full 360° orbit navigation. Suits product configurators, architectural visualization, digital-twin dashboards, or scientific/engineering data portals where LiDAR or photogrammetry scan data needs to be presented interactively.
usageNote: Wrap the entire init/render logic in a useEffect with a canvas ref in React/Next.js. Replace renderer.domElement appending with a ref to a <canvas> or <div> container. Supply PCD files via your own CDN or public directory and pass their URLs to PCDLoader.load() instead of the hardcoded './models/pcd/' paths. Use react-three-fiber's <points> primitive as an alternative to skip boilerplate. Clean up via a useEffect return function that calls renderer.dispose() and controls.dispose().
constraints: Requires WebGL2-capable GPU; large PCD files (millions of points) can be heavy on mobile GPUs and consume significant memory. The OrbitControls render-on-demand pattern (no animation loop) is efficient but demands careful event wiring. Not suitable for very low-end or older mobile devices. PCD files must be served with correct CORS headers if hosted cross-origin.
antiPatterns: Forgetting to call renderer.dispose() and geometry.dispose() on unmount causes GPU memory leaks. Hardcoding window.innerWidth/innerHeight instead of reading the container element dimensions breaks embedded/component use. Calling render() in multiple event listeners simultaneously without debouncing can cause unnecessary redraws. Not calling gui.destroy() before recreating it when switching point clouds leaves orphaned GUI panels.
accessibilityNotes: The canvas has no ARIA role or label by default; add aria-label describing the scanned object. Provide a static screenshot fallback for users with reduced-motion preferences or when WebGL is unavailable. The GUI controls are keyboard-operable in lil-gui but ensure tab focus is not trapped inside the canvas. Screen readers cannot interpret point cloud data; supplement with a text description of the object shown.

technique: interactive 3D molecular structure viewer with CSS2D atom labels
description: Renders color-coded 3D molecular structures with labeled atoms and connecting bonds that can be rotated freely in 3D space, suitable for science education platforms, pharmaceutical product pages, chemistry learning tools, or any site needing interactive data-driven 3D visualization.
usageNote: Wrap in a useEffect with a canvas ref in React/Next.js; create the WebGLRenderer targeting the ref element rather than appending to a container div. Also mount the CSS2DRenderer's domElement inside the same wrapper div with position:absolute. PDB files must be hosted on your own server or CDN (replace 'models/pdb/' with your public asset path, e.g. '/public/pdb/' in Next.js or a CDN URL). Use react-three-fiber with @react-three/drei's Html component as an alternative for cleaner React integration of the CSS2D labels.
constraints: Requires WebGL renderer with antialiasing; CSS2DRenderer must be layered on top as a separate DOM element. Moderate GPU cost scales with molecular complexity (e.g. Buckyball or Graphite are heavier). Mobile support is feasible but TrackballControls touch handling can conflict with page scroll gestures. Not suitable for very low-end devices or contexts requiring SSR without a canvas polyfill.
antiPatterns: Forgetting to dispose geometries and materials when switching molecules causes memory leaks — always traverse and call dispose on meshes and materials before loading a new model. Forgetting to resize both the WebGLRenderer AND the CSS2DRenderer on window resize causes label misalignment. Hardcoding window.innerWidth/innerHeight breaks layout in embedded or modal contexts — use the container element's offsetWidth/offsetHeight instead. Leaving the animation loop running after component unmount causes memory leaks in React.
accessibilityNotes: The 3D canvas is not screen-reader accessible; provide a text description or data table of the molecule's atomic composition as a visually-hidden fallback. For reduced-motion preferences, disable the auto-rotate or continuous animation loop and only render on user interaction. Keyboard navigation is not supported by TrackballControls; consider adding keyboard shortcuts or a static image fallback for accessibility compliance.

technique: PLY 3D model viewer with orbiting camera and shadow casting
description: Renders high-detail 3D mesh models loaded from PLY files (supporting both ASCII and binary formats) on a fog-filled ground plane with multi-light shadow casting and a slow automated camera orbit. Suits portfolio showcases, product visualization landing pages, science or engineering sites displaying scan data, or museum/cultural heritage websites displaying 3D artifacts.
usageNote: Wrap initialization in a useEffect with a canvas ref; create the renderer with the ref element instead of appending to document.body. In react-three-fiber, use <primitive> with geometry loaded via PLYLoader inside a useLoader or useEffect call. Replace hardcoded './models/ply/...' paths with URLs served from your /public folder (Next.js) or a CDN; pass the URL as a prop so the component is reusable. Cancel the animation loop and dispose geometry/material/renderer in the useEffect cleanup function.
constraints: Requires WebGL with shadow map support; binary PLY files can be large (Lucy100k is ~2MB) so lazy-load or stream them. Mobile GPUs may struggle with high-polygon PLY meshes and shadow maps simultaneously. Not suitable for low-end devices without LOD or polygon reduction. PLYLoader does not support animations, only static geometry.
antiPatterns: Forgetting to call geometry.dispose() and material.dispose() when the component unmounts causes GPU memory leaks. Hardcoding window.innerWidth/window.innerHeight instead of the container element's size breaks embedded or partial-page layouts. Not calling renderer.dispose() on cleanup. Loading multi-MB PLY files synchronously without a loading indicator blocks perceived performance. Forgetting to update camera.aspect on resize produces distorted output.
accessibilityNotes: Add a prefers-reduced-motion media query check to pause or disable the camera orbit animation; a static first-frame render or a flat 2D image of the model should serve as a fallback. The canvas has no inherent keyboard or screen reader semantics — add role='img' and an aria-label describing the 3D content. Provide a text alternative describing the featured object for screen reader users.

technique: STL model viewer with orbiting camera and Phong shading
description: Renders one or more STL 3D models (both ASCII and binary formats, including vertex-colored variants) on a ground plane with atmospheric fog and a slow auto-orbiting camera. Suits product pages, engineering portfolios, manufacturing showcases, or any site that needs to display user-uploaded or pre-packaged 3D geometry without a full CAD viewer.
usageNote: Wrap the entire init/animate block inside a React useEffect with a canvas ref, or use react-three-fiber with a <Canvas> component. Replace the STLLoader.load() calls with URLs pointing to your own CDN-hosted or public-folder STL files (e.g. /models/part.stl in Next.js public/). Clean up with renderer.dispose() and cancelAnimationFrame in the useEffect return. The Stats panel should be removed in production.
constraints: Requires WebGL support; STL files can be large so network load time matters — binary STL is preferred over ASCII for size. The auto-orbit animation and shadow maps add moderate GPU cost; on low-end mobile, disable shadows and reduce pixel ratio. Does not support animated meshes or PBR materials out of the box.
antiPatterns: Forgetting to call geometry.dispose() and material.dispose() when the component unmounts, leading to memory leaks. Hardcoding window.innerWidth/innerHeight instead of measuring the parent container, which breaks embedded use inside a page section. Not handling the async nature of STLLoader.load() — trying to manipulate the mesh before the callback fires. Leaving the Stats overlay visible in production builds.
accessibilityNotes: The scene is a purely decorative 3D canvas with no keyboard or screen-reader access. Provide an aria-hidden='true' attribute on the canvas and a visible static image or descriptive text alternative for users who cannot perceive 3D content. Respect prefers-reduced-motion by stopping the camera orbit (freeze camera.position) when the media query matches.

technique: SVG-to-3D mesh renderer with fill and stroke geometry extraction
description: Parses SVG files and renders them as interactive 3D meshes in a WebGL scene, with separate fill and stroke geometry layers that can be toggled or viewed in wireframe. Suits portfolio sites, logo showcases, data visualization headers, or any product page that wants to elevate flat vector artwork into an explorable 3D object.
usageNote: Wrap in a React useEffect with a canvas ref: create renderer targeting the ref, set up OrbitControls, and call the loadSVG logic inside the effect. Return a cleanup function that calls renderer.dispose() and removes the canvas. Replace local asset paths (e.g. models/svg/tiger.svg) with paths inside your public/ folder (Next.js) or src/assets/ (Vite), or fetch them from a CDN URL. In react-three-fiber use a useLoader(SVGLoader, url) hook inside a component and map paths to ShapeGeometry meshes.
constraints: Requires WebGL renderer; not suitable for CSS-only or canvas-2D fallback. Each SVG path becomes one or more Mesh objects, so complex SVGs with hundreds of paths can generate many draw calls — profile for mobile. OrbitControls adds pointer-event overhead. Best for decorative hero or section backgrounds rather than repeated UI elements.
antiPatterns: Forgetting to call disposeScene (dispose geometry and material for every mesh) before loading a new SVG causes memory leaks. Hardcoding window.innerWidth/innerHeight breaks in embedded or partial-page contexts — always derive size from the container element. Not inverting the Y scale (group.scale.y *= -1) produces upside-down SVGs. Omitting renderOrder on meshes causes z-fighting between fill and stroke layers.
accessibilityNotes: The 3D canvas is purely decorative; provide an aria-hidden='true' attribute on the canvas element and include a visible static SVG or descriptive alt text alongside it. Respect prefers-reduced-motion by disabling OrbitControls auto-rotate and skipping any animation loop, falling back to a single static render() call. Ensure keyboard users cannot get trapped in OrbitControls by setting controls.enabled = false when the canvas is not focused.

technique: GPU-compressed texture showcase on 3D geometry with cubemap reflections
description: Displays a grid of rotating 3D boxes and a torus, each skinned with a different GPU-compressed texture format (DXT1/3/5, BC6H, ARGB) and environment-mapped reflections from a compressed cubemap. Suitable for a graphics-tech product page, a game-asset pipeline tool, or any site section that needs high-performance textured 3D objects rendered at scale.
usageNote: Wrap the entire init/animate block inside a React useEffect with a canvas ref, returning a cleanup function that calls renderer.dispose(). In Next.js, gate the import behind a dynamic() with ssr:false because DDSLoader uses browser APIs. Replace all local DDS asset paths with your own CDN URLs or public-folder paths; the DDSLoader.load() call accepts any URL string.
constraints: Requires WebGL with S3TC/DXT extension support (WEBGL_compressed_texture_s3tc); BC6H requires EXT_texture_compression_bptc. Most desktop GPUs support DXT; mobile WebGL support for DXT varies and BC6H is rarely available on mobile. Performance is excellent once textures are uploaded since GPU-compressed formats reduce VRAM bandwidth significantly.
antiPatterns: Forgetting to call renderer.dispose(), texture.dispose(), and geometry.dispose() on unmount causes GPU memory leaks. Hardcoding window.innerWidth/innerHeight instead of using the canvas container's clientWidth/clientHeight breaks responsive layouts. Assuming DXT or BC6H is always available without checking renderer.extensions.get() leads to silent black textures. Not setting colorSpace on loaded textures causes washed-out or over-bright colours.
accessibilityNotes: Provide a static fallback image for users with prefers-reduced-motion or when WebGL is unavailable. The canvas has no inherent keyboard focus or screen-reader semantics; add aria-hidden='true' and a visually-hidden text description of the content being displayed. Stop the animation loop when the tab is hidden using the Page Visibility API.

technique: HDR/EXR image display with adjustable tone mapping exposure
description: Renders a high dynamic range EXR image fullscreen using Reinhard tone mapping with a user-adjustable exposure slider, producing photorealistic luminance reproduction. Suits photography portfolios, architecture visualization sites, product showcases, or any context requiring accurate HDR image presentation.
usageNote: In React/Next.js, wrap renderer setup in a useEffect with a canvas ref and return a cleanup function that calls renderer.dispose(). For react-three-fiber, use the <Canvas> component with toneMapping and toneMappingExposure props on the gl object, and load the EXR via useLoader(EXRLoader, url). Replace the local 'textures/memorial.exr' path with a URL from your public folder, CDN, or CMS asset pipeline. Expose the exposure parameter via React state if you want a UI slider.
constraints: Requires WebGL 2 or WebGL 1 with appropriate extensions for float textures; EXR decoding is CPU-intensive on first load so large files may cause frame drops. Mobile GPUs with limited float texture support may show degraded results or fail silently. Not suitable for low-end devices or situations where bundle size is critical, as EXRLoader adds non-trivial weight.
antiPatterns: Forgetting to dispose the EXR texture and plane geometry on component unmount causing memory leaks; hardcoding window.innerWidth/innerHeight instead of using the container element's dimensions; omitting the resize handler causing distortion on orientation change; applying mipmapping to NPOT EXR textures which three.js disables by default for good reason — do not override minFilter without testing.
accessibilityNotes: Provide a static fallback JPEG or PNG version of the HDR image as a standard img element for users with reduced-motion preferences or when WebGL is unavailable. The exposure control slider should be keyboard-accessible and labeled with ARIA attributes if exposed in the UI. Screen readers receive no meaningful content from the canvas, so add an aria-label or visually hidden description of the image subject.

technique: HDR image viewer with tone mapping exposure control
description: Displays a high dynamic range (HDR) photograph or panorama with real-time Reinhard tone mapping and adjustable exposure, rendering photorealistic lighting depth on a flat plane. Suits photography portfolios, architectural visualization previews, or product pages that need to showcase high-fidelity imagery with true luminance data.
usageNote: In React or Next.js, mount inside a useEffect with a canvas ref: create the renderer targeting the ref element rather than appending to document.body, and clean up on unmount by calling renderer.dispose(). With react-three-fiber use a <Canvas> with a custom tone mapping config and load the HDR via useLoader(HDRLoader, url). Replace 'textures/memorial.hdr' with a CDN-hosted .hdr file URL or a path inside your /public folder (e.g. '/textures/your-image.hdr' in Next.js).
constraints: Requires WebGL renderer with tone mapping support; .hdr files are large (often 5–30 MB) so network load time must be managed with a loading state. Not suitable for low-bandwidth or mobile-first contexts without aggressive compression or EXR alternatives. GPU cost is low once loaded since the scene is a static quad.
antiPatterns: Forgetting to call texture.dispose() and renderer.dispose() on component unmount causing memory leaks; hardcoding window.innerWidth/innerHeight instead of using the container element's dimensions; not handling the async load callback with a loading indicator, leaving a blank canvas; failing to update camera frustum on resize leading to distorted aspect ratio.
accessibilityNotes: Provide a static fallback tag with an equivalent JPEG/PNG version of the HDR scene for users with reduced motion or when WebGL is unavailable. Add an aria-label or visually hidden caption describing the image content. The exposure slider should be keyboard accessible with proper label and role attributes if exposed in the UI.

technique: GPU-compressed texture loading with device-capability detection across PVRTC, S3TC, ETC1/2, and ASTC formats
description: Rotating 3D cubes textured with GPU-native compressed textures, automatically selecting the optimal format (BC1/BC3 for desktop, PVRTC for iOS, ETC1/ASTC for Android). Suited for performance-critical product viewers, game asset previews, or any 3D content section that needs fast texture streaming across device types.
usageNote: Wrap the renderer, scene, camera, and animation loop in a useEffect with a canvas ref in React/Next.js. Use renderer.domElement appended to the ref instead of document.body. Replace the KTX texture asset paths with your own hosted KTX files (served from /public or a CDN). The device-capability detection (formats.pvrtc, formats.s3tc, etc.) is the core portable logic and should be kept intact. Consider using react-three-fiber's useThree and useLoader with a custom KTX loader for a more idiomatic R3F approach.
constraints: Requires WebGL renderer; compressed texture support is hardware-dependent and detected at runtime — not all formats will be available on all devices. KTX files must be pre-authored for each target format (BC1, BC3, PVRTC, ETC1, ASTC), which adds build pipeline complexity. Not suitable if only a single texture format can be produced. Works on mobile but PVRTC is iOS-only and ETC1 is Android-only.
antiPatterns: Hardcoding a single texture format without capability detection will silently fail or render a black surface on unsupported devices. Forgetting to set colorSpace = SRGBColorSpace on color maps causes washed-out colors. Skipping disposal of KTX textures and geometry on component unmount causes GPU memory leaks. Hardcoding window.innerWidth/innerHeight instead of the container element's dimensions breaks layout in embedded canvases.
accessibilityNotes: The animation loop (rotating cubes) should be paused when prefers-reduced-motion is set; replace the rotation update with a static render call. Provide a static fallback image for screen readers via an aria-label on the canvas or a visually-hidden description. The scene has no keyboard-interactive elements, so no focus management is required, but the canvas should have role='img' and a descriptive aria-label.

technique: KTX2 GPU texture format comparison gallery with scissored multi-scene rendering
description: Displays a scrollable grid of flat image planes, each rendered in an isolated WebGL viewport, showcasing the same texture across different GPU compression formats (uncompressed, BCn, ASTC, Basis Universal). Suited for asset pipeline documentation, texture tool dashboards, or any web app that needs to display and compare image assets loaded from optimized GPU texture files.
usageNote: In React/Next.js, initialize the renderer and KTX2Loader inside a useEffect with a canvas ref, and return a cleanup function that calls renderer.dispose(). Replace the local 'textures/ktx2/' path with your own CDN or public folder URL passed to loader.setPath(). For react-three-fiber, use a custom loader hook with useLoader or a manual useEffect; the scissored multi-scene pattern is easier to replicate with vanilla Three.js than with R3F's single-scene model. The KTX2Loader requires the Basis transcoder WASM/JS files to be hosted and referenced via loader.setTranscoderPath().
constraints: Requires WebGL2 for many compressed formats; GPU-native compressed formats vary by device (ASTC on mobile, BCn on desktop), so Basis Universal (ETC1S/UASTC) is the safest cross-device choice. The scissored multi-canvas approach has low overhead per tile but scales poorly past ~50 simultaneous scenes. Not suitable for environments where WebGL2 is unavailable.
antiPatterns: Forgetting to call loader.detectSupport(renderer) before loading, which causes silent failures on unsupported formats. Not hosting the Basis transcoder WASM files alongside the app. Reusing a single renderer without scissor/viewport management leading to scenes overwriting each other. Failing to dispose textures and geometries when the component unmounts, causing GPU memory leaks. Hardcoding canvas dimensions instead of responding to ResizeObserver.
accessibilityNotes: Each texture panel should have an aria-label or visually hidden caption describing the format and color space. Provide a static fallback or descriptive text for screen readers. No motion is inherent to the scene, so reduced-motion users are unaffected. Keyboard navigation should allow tabbing through format cards if they are interactive.

technique: Lottie animation as live canvas texture mapped onto a rotating 3D rounded box
description: A glossy, rounded cube slowly auto-rotates in a dark studio environment while its surface displays a looping Lottie vector animation rendered in real time as a WebGL texture. Suits product showcases, brand intros, interactive loading screens, or 'about' sections on creative or SaaS websites.
usageNote: Wrap the entire init block inside a useEffect with a canvas ref, attaching the renderer to the ref element instead of document.body. Install lottie-web via npm and import it directly rather than from the CDN. Replace the local Lottie JSON path (textures/lottie/...) with an import or a public-folder URL to your own Lottie animation JSON file. Clean up by calling renderer.dispose() and controls.dispose() in the useEffect return. With react-three-fiber, use a useTexture hook pattern alongside a useEffect that drives the CanvasTexture update on each lottie enterFrame event.
constraints: Requires WebGL 1 or 2; works on modern mobile browsers but Lottie canvas rendering plus WebGL texture uploads are CPU-intensive and may drop frames on low-end mobile devices. The hidden off-screen Lottie canvas must remain in the DOM (only display:none) or the canvas context is lost. Not suitable for extremely performance-constrained environments or SSR without a browser canvas polyfill.
antiPatterns: Forgetting to set texture.needsUpdate = true on every Lottie enterFrame event will freeze the texture. Removing the container from the DOM entirely (vs display:none) destroys the canvas context. Hardcoding window.innerWidth/innerHeight instead of the container element dimensions breaks embedded or non-fullscreen layouts. Not disposing the PMREMGenerator texture causes GPU memory leaks. Neglecting to call animation.destroy() on unmount leaks the Lottie instance.
accessibilityNotes: Respect prefers-reduced-motion by pausing or stopping the Lottie animation and disabling OrbitControls autoRotate when the media query matches. Provide a static fallback image (e.g. a poster PNG of the brand mark) for users who cannot run WebGL. The 3D canvas has no inherent semantic meaning, so add aria-hidden='true' to the canvas element and convey the same brand message via visible text or an accessible heading nearby.

technique: PVR compressed texture mapping on rotating 3D objects with cube environment reflection
description: A grid of rotating 3D cubes and tori each displaying different GPU-compressed (PVR) textures including opaque, transparent, mipmapped, and cube-map reflective surfaces. Best suited for showcasing high-performance texture rendering in product configurators, game asset previews, or mobile-optimized 3D showcases where GPU memory is a constraint.
usageNote: Port into React/Next.js using a useEffect hook with a canvas ref or via react-three-fiber. Replace PVRLoader with a standard TextureLoader or KTX2Loader if PVR is not available; alternatively host your own .pvr files and update the loader.load() paths to your CDN or public/ folder URLs. Wrap renderer creation and the animation loop inside useEffect, and return a cleanup function that calls renderer.dispose() and cancelAnimationFrame.
constraints: PVR texture support (PVRTC compression) is primarily a PowerVR GPU feature, best supported on Apple iOS/macOS devices and some Android GPUs; on desktop WebGL contexts without PVRTC extension support textures may silently fall back or fail to render. Verify WEBGL_compressed_texture_pvrtc extension availability before using. Not suitable for projects requiring universal cross-platform texture support without fallbacks.
antiPatterns: Forgetting to check for PVRTC GPU extension support before loading PVR files leading to invisible or broken textures. Not disposing of CompressedTexture objects and geometry on component unmount causing GPU memory leaks. Hardcoding window.innerWidth/innerHeight instead of using the canvas container's dimensions. Skipping colorSpace assignment which causes washed-out or overly bright colors.
accessibilityNotes: Continuous rotation animation should be paused or replaced with a static render when the prefers-reduced-motion media query is active. Provide a static fallback image for contexts where WebGL is unavailable. All 3D content is purely decorative so no keyboard focus or screen reader description is required, but add aria-hidden='true' to the canvas element.

technique: TGA texture-mapped 3D box with orbit controls
description: Two textured 3D cubes side by side in a lit scene, demonstrating TGA-format image textures applied to geometry. Suitable for product configurators, 3D asset previews, or game-asset showcase sections on a portfolio or e-commerce site.
usageNote: In React/Next.js, wrap the init logic inside a useEffect with a canvas ref (or use react-three-fiber with a <mesh> and <meshPhongMaterial map={...}>). Replace local .tga paths (textures/crate_grey8.tga, textures/crate_color8.tga) with your own assets hosted in /public or a CDN; TGALoader accepts any accessible URL. Ensure OrbitControls is imported from the same addons path or its r3f equivalent (@react-three/drei's OrbitControls).
constraints: Requires WebGL renderer; TGA decoding happens on the CPU via TGALoader so avoid large TGA files on mobile to prevent jank. TGA is rarely used on the web — consider converting assets to WebP or PNG unless TGA is a hard requirement from a pipeline. Works on all modern browsers with WebGL support.
antiPatterns: Forgetting to call geometry.dispose() and texture.dispose() on unmount in React, causing memory leaks. Hardcoding window.innerWidth/innerHeight instead of using the parent container dimensions, which breaks embedded layouts. Not setting texture.colorSpace = THREE.SRGBColorSpace causing washed-out colours. Neglecting to remove the resize event listener on cleanup.
accessibilityNotes: The canvas has no semantic meaning to screen readers; add an aria-label or visually-hidden description of the 3D content. Provide a static fallback image for users with reduced-motion preferences or on devices where WebGL is unavailable. Orbit interaction is mouse/touch-driven with no keyboard equivalent by default — consider adding keyboard controls or disabling the interaction entirely for accessibility.

technique: TIFF texture loading onto flat planes with multiple compression format support
description: Three flat textured quads are displayed side by side, each loaded from a TIFF image using different compression variants (uncompressed, LZW, JPEG-in-TIFF). Suits archival asset viewers, print-production pipelines, CAD/design tool web frontends, or any site needing to render professional-grade TIFF imagery sourced from photography or design workflows directly in the browser.
usageNote: In React or Next.js, wrap initialization in a useEffect with a canvas ref: create the renderer targeting the ref element instead of appending to document.body, and return a cleanup function that calls renderer.dispose(). Replace local .tif asset paths with your own hosted TIFF URLs (CDN, S3, etc.) or import them via a bundler plugin that serves static assets. In react-three-fiber, use useLoader with TIFFLoader and apply the texture to a meshBasicMaterial map prop.
constraints: Requires WebGL renderer (no WebGPU fallback). TIFFLoader is a non-trivial addon that parses TIFF binary in JS, so load times for large or uncompressed TIFFs can be high. Mobile support is fine for small TIFFs but large uncompressed files may exceed GPU texture size limits on low-end devices. Only baseline TIFF compression types (uncompressed, LZW, JPEG) are supported—multi-page or 16-bit TIFFs may not render correctly.
antiPatterns: Forgetting to set texture.colorSpace = THREE.SRGBColorSpace causes washed-out colors. Not disposing textures and materials when components unmount causes memory leaks. Hardcoding window.innerWidth/innerHeight instead of using the container element dimensions breaks layout in embedded or partial-page contexts. Failing to handle async load order before calling render() can result in blank frames.

technique: Ultra HDR equirectangular environment map with PBR metallic object
description: A high-dynamic-range panoramic environment lights and reflects off a slowly rotating metallic 3D object, producing photorealistic reflections and accurate exposure. Ideal for product showcases, jewelry or luxury goods landing pages, automotive configurators, or any hero section demanding premium material rendering.
usageNote: Wrap renderer creation and animation loop inside a useEffect with a canvas ref in React/Next.js, returning a cleanup function that calls renderer.dispose() and cancelAnimationFrame. Use react-three-fiber alternatively for declarative setup. Replace the local 'textures/equirectangular/spruit_sunrise_${resolution}.hdr.jpg' paths with your own CDN-hosted UltraHDR .hdr.jpg files or any equirectangular HDR environment map loaded via UltraHDRLoader or RGBELoader. Remove the lil-gui panel and wire exposure/metalness/roughness to your own UI controls or hardcode them.
constraints: Requires WebGL with floating-point texture support (OES_texture_float or OES_texture_half_float); FloatType textures may fail on low-end mobile GPUs so HalfFloatType is the safer default. Downloading a 4k HDR image is heavy (often 5–20 MB); use the 2k variant on mobile or lazy-load on demand. Not suitable for contexts where WebGL is unavailable or canvas rendering is blocked.
antiPatterns: Forgetting to call texture.dispose() and renderer.dispose() on unmount causes GPU memory leaks. Hardcoding window.innerWidth/innerHeight instead of the container element's dimensions breaks layouts inside non-full-page canvases. Loading FloatType textures without checking GPU capability causes silent fallback or rendering errors. Not removing the resize event listener on cleanup causes stale callbacks.
accessibilityNotes: Respect prefers-reduced-motion by setting autoRotate to false when the media query matches. Provide a static high-quality PNG or WebP fallback image for users with JS disabled or WebGL unavailable. The 3D canvas has no inherent semantic meaning, so add an aria-label describing the product being showcased and ensure surrounding page content is fully keyboard navigable without relying on OrbitControls interaction.

technique: 3D extruded text with mirror reflection and drag-to-rotate interaction, loaded from a custom TTF font
description: Glossy, beveled 3D letters float above a semi-transparent plane with a mirrored reflection below, set against a dark fogged background. Ideal for hero sections, brand splash screens, product launch pages, or interactive typographic statements where a dramatic first impression is needed.
usageNote: In React/Next.js, wrap all init logic in a useEffect with a canvas ref and return a cleanup function that calls renderer.dispose() and removes event listeners. Use react-three-fiber's <Canvas> with @react-three/drei's <Text3D> component as a higher-level alternative. Replace the TTF font path ('fonts/ttf/kenpixel.ttf') with a URL pointing to your own hosted font file (e.g., in /public in Next.js) or a CDN-hosted TTF; pass the URL string to TTFLoader.load().
constraints: Requires WebGL with decent GPU for smooth rendering; TextGeometry is CPU-heavy so avoid regenerating it on every keystroke without debouncing. Mobile performs adequately for static display but interactive typing input is impractical. Not suitable for very long strings due to geometry cost. Requires WebGL renderer — no WebGPU or CSS fallback.
antiPatterns: Forgetting to call textGeo.dispose() and removing old meshes before creating new ones on text refresh, causing memory leaks. Hardcoding window.innerWidth/window.innerHeight instead of using a container ref for responsive sizing. Omitting debounce on text input causing geometry thrashing. Not removing pointermove/pointerup event listeners on cleanup. Assuming the TTF loads synchronously before createText() is called.
accessibilityNotes: The 3D text is purely visual with no semantic HTML equivalent — always provide an accessible <h1> or aria-label with the same text content off-screen. Respect prefers-reduced-motion by disabling the rotation animation and drag interaction. Keyboard-typed text input lacks a visible text cursor or ARIA live region; add one for screen reader announcements. On low-end or no-WebGL devices, provide a static styled text fallback.

technique: USDZ 3D model viewer with HDR environment lighting and orbit controls
description: Renders a photorealistic 3D product or object loaded from a USDZ file, set against a blurred HDR equirectangular environment that provides realistic image-based lighting and reflections. Ideal for e-commerce product pages, luxury brand showcases, or portfolio sites that need to display high-fidelity 3D assets with interactive 360-degree inspection.
usageNote: In React or Next.js, wrap initialization in a useEffect with a canvas ref and add a cleanup function that calls renderer.dispose() and removes the event listener. Alternatively use react-three-fiber with useLoader(USDLoader, url). Replace 'models/usdz/saeukkang.usdz' with a URL to your own USDZ asset (e.g. hosted on a CDN or served from /public), and replace 'textures/equirectangular/venice_sunset_1k.hdr' with your own HDR environment map URL.
constraints: Requires WebGL 1 or 2 with reasonable GPU support; USDZ parsing is CPU-intensive and may cause a loading delay on mobile — show a loading spinner. USDZ files can be large, so lazy-load behind user interaction or Intersection Observer. Not suitable for very low-end mobile devices or environments where WebGL is unavailable.
antiPatterns: Forgetting to call renderer.dispose() and geometry/material cleanup on component unmount causing memory leaks; hardcoding window.innerWidth/window.innerHeight instead of using the container element's dimensions; not handling async load errors (network failure or unsupported USDZ features); omitting the resize observer so the canvas stays at its initial size after layout changes.
accessibilityNotes: Provide a static hero image fallback for users with prefers-reduced-motion or no WebGL support. Add an aria-label to the canvas element describing the 3D object (e.g. 'Interactive 3D view of [product name]'). Keyboard users cannot orbit by default — consider adding keyboard-driven rotation via OrbitControls key bindings or providing alternative product views as images.

technique: interactive voxel model viewer with orbit controls
description: Renders a full-color 3D voxel model (like a pixelated building or game asset) that users can rotate and inspect from all angles. Ideal for portfolio showcases, game asset previews, NFT or collectible displays, or any site wanting a retro-pixel 3D aesthetic.
usageNote: In React/Next.js, wrap the setup in a useEffect hook with a canvas ref and return a cleanup function that calls renderer.dispose() and removes the DOM element. For react-three-fiber, use @react-three/fiber with a useLoader(VOXLoader, url) pattern inside a Canvas component. Replace the hardcoded local .vox path with a URL pointing to your own hosted asset (e.g., a CDN path or a Next.js /public folder route like '/models/monu10.vox'). The VOXLoader addon must still be imported from three/addons.
constraints: Requires WebGL support; the VOXLoader parses binary .vox files so the asset must be served with correct MIME types. Large voxel models with many chunks can be geometry-heavy so test on mid-range mobile. OrbitControls adds JS overhead on every frame. Not suitable for environments where three.js addons cannot be bundled (e.g., some CDN-only setups without a bundler).
antiPatterns: Forgetting to call renderer.dispose() and geometry/material dispose on unmount causes memory leaks in SPAs. Not handling the async loader callback before component unmount can cause setState-on-unmounted errors. Hardcoding window.innerWidth/window.innerHeight instead of measuring the container element breaks layout in embedded or partial-page scenarios. Forgetting to update camera.aspect and call updateProjectionMatrix on resize produces a stretched view.
accessibilityNotes: The 3D canvas is not screen-reader accessible; add an aria-label or visually hidden description of the model for assistive technologies. Provide a static screenshot fallback via a <noscript> tag or CSS for users with reduced-motion preferences or no WebGL support. Respect prefers-reduced-motion by disabling auto-rotation if added, though this example is interaction-driven so risk is lower.

technique: VRML 3D model loader with orbit controls and asset switcher
description: Renders legacy VRML (.wrl) 3D models in an interactive 3D viewport with orbit camera controls, supporting geometry types including meshes, lines, points, textures, and extrusions. Suited for digital archives, heritage preservation sites, engineering documentation portals, or any platform needing to display legacy 3D CAD or virtual-reality assets in the browser.
usageNote: Wrap the entire init/animate logic inside a useEffect hook with a canvas ref, passing the ref's current element to the WebGLRenderer constructor instead of appending to document.body. Replace 'models/vrml/' paths with URLs pointing to VRML files served from your public directory, a CDN, or a signed blob storage URL. In Next.js ensure the import is dynamic with ssr:false. For react-three-fiber, use a useLoader hook with VRMLLoader once r3f supports it, or fall back to the imperative pattern inside useEffect.
constraints: Requires WebGL renderer; not suitable for server-side rendering. VRML files can be large and parse slowly on mobile — test with your actual assets. The loader is CPU-bound during parse so large scenes may cause frame drops. Mobile GPU support is generally fine but complex VRML geometry with many draw calls may degrade on low-end devices.
antiPatterns: Forgetting to dispose geometries, materials, and textures when switching assets will cause GPU memory leaks — the traverse-and-dispose pattern in the GUI onChange handler must be preserved. Hardcoding window.innerWidth/innerHeight instead of using a container element's dimensions breaks embedded viewports. Not calling controls.update() in the animation loop disables damping. Serving VRML files with the wrong MIME type will silently fail the load.
accessibilityNotes: The 3D canvas is not screen-reader accessible; add an aria-label on the canvas and provide a text description or static screenshot fallback for users who cannot interact with 3D. Respect prefers-reduced-motion by pausing auto-rotation or disabling damping animations. Keyboard orbit control is not provided out of the box — consider adding keyboard event listeners for accessibility.

technique: rotating 3D point cloud from XYZ molecular data
description: A slowly rotating cloud of 3D points derived from scientific coordinate data, rendering as a glowing particle structure in space. Ideal for science, biotech, research, or data visualization websites that want to convey molecular structure, genomics, or spatial data in a visually compelling hero or background section.
usageNote: In React/Next.js, move all init logic into a useEffect hook with a canvas ref passed to WebGLRenderer instead of appending to document.body. Clean up with renderer.dispose() and cancelAnimationFrame on unmount. Replace the local 'models/xyz/helix_201.xyz' path with a URL pointing to an XYZ file hosted in your public/ directory or a CDN. If using react-three-fiber, use useLoader with a custom XYZLoader registration or load the geometry imperatively inside useEffect.
constraints: Requires WebGL renderer; no WebGPU fallback provided. Point cloud rendering is GPU-friendly and performs well on mid-range mobile devices as long as point count stays below ~100k. XYZLoader is a lightweight addon but the XYZ file itself must be served from an accessible URL. Not suitable for contexts requiring server-side rendering without a canvas polyfill.
antiPatterns: Forgetting to call geometry.dispose() and material.dispose() on component unmount causes GPU memory leaks. Hardcoding window.innerWidth/innerHeight breaks in embedded or multi-panel layouts — use the container element's dimensions instead. Omitting the resize listener causes distorted aspect ratios on orientation change. Not handling the async load callback can cause null reference errors if the component unmounts before the file loads.
accessibilityNotes: The rotating animation provides no semantic information; add an aria-hidden='true' attribute to the canvas and a visually hidden description for screen readers. Respect prefers-reduced-motion by checking the media query and setting rotation delta to 0 or pausing the animation loop. Provide a static fallback image for users with no WebGL support using a <noscript> or a canvas context detection check.

technique: level-of-detail (LOD) 3D object field with fly-through navigation
description: A vast, fog-shrouded 3D field of thousands of glowing wireframe spheres that automatically swap to lower-polygon versions as the camera moves away, enabling smooth fly-through navigation. Suits space exploration UIs, data visualization dashboards, sci-fi hero sections, or interactive product configurators that need dense 3D scenes.
usageNote: In React/Next.js, initialize the scene inside a useEffect with a canvas ref and return a cleanup function that disposes renderer, geometry, and controls. With react-three-fiber, use the <LOD> component from @react-three/drei and <FlyControls> from the same package. No local assets are referenced, so no path replacement is needed. Pass the canvas ref to renderer.domElement and attach FlyControls to it.
constraints: Rendering 1000 LOD objects is GPU-moderate on desktop but can be heavy on low-end mobile GPUs; reduce object count to 200-300 for mobile. Requires WebGL 1 at minimum. FlyControls use keyboard+mouse input which conflicts with scroll on mobile — consider replacing with OrbitControls or touch-friendly alternatives for mobile contexts.
antiPatterns: Forgetting to call renderer.dispose() and geometry[i][0].dispose() on unmount causing memory leaks; not detaching the resize event listener; hardcoding window.innerWidth/innerHeight instead of reading from a container element; omitting lod.matrixAutoUpdate = false which causes per-frame matrix recalculation overhead; not updating camera.aspect on resize.
accessibilityNotes: Add a prefers-reduced-motion media query check and either pause the animation loop or replace with a static rendered image. FlyControls are keyboard-driven (WASD/arrows) but provide no visible focus indicators — add aria-label to the canvas and a skip-link. Screen readers receive no scene content; provide a meaningful aria-label or visually hidden description of the scene purpose.

technique: animated metaball / marching cubes isosurface with multiple material presets
description: Smoothly animated organic blob shapes that merge and separate in real time, rendered with a variety of surface materials including metallic, chrome, liquid-refraction, toon, and hatching shaders. Suits creative agency hero sections, product configurators, generative art portfolios, or science/biology visualization pages that need a striking, living 3D centerpiece.
usageNote: Wrap in a React useEffect with a canvas ref and a cleanup function that calls renderer.dispose() and removes the animation loop. Replace the cube environment map (textures/cube/SwedishRoyalCastle/) with your own CubeTextureLoader URLs or a PMREMGenerator-baked HDR; replace textures/uv_grid_opengl.jpg with any tiling texture. In react-three-fiber, use useFrame for the animation loop and import MarchingCubes from the addons path. Remove lil-gui and Stats from production builds.
constraints: Requires WebGL 1 or 2; the marching cubes resolution (default 28) is the main performance knob — raising it above 40 becomes GPU-heavy on mid-range mobile. Toon/hatching shader variants are cheap; reflective/refractive envMap variants require cube texture assets. Not suitable for very low-end devices or WebGL-unavailable contexts.
antiPatterns: Forgetting to call effect.reset() each frame before re-adding balls causes geometry accumulation. Not disposing MarchingCubes geometry and all material instances on unmount causes memory leaks. Hardcoding window.innerWidth/window.innerHeight instead of using a ResizeObserver on the container breaks layout in embedded or responsive contexts. Importing cube texture URLs that do not exist will silently produce a black envMap.
accessibilityNotes: Add a prefers-reduced-motion media query check and pause or stop the animation loop if the user prefers reduced motion; show a static rendered screenshot as a CSS background-image fallback. The canvas has no semantic content, so add aria-hidden='true' and provide a visually hidden description for screen readers. No keyboard interaction is required for a decorative hero use case, but if orbit controls are exposed, ensure focus management and keyboard panning are documented.

technique: alpha-hash transparency with TAA anti-aliasing on instanced 3D objects
description: A 3D grid of semi-transparent, randomly colored icosahedral spheres rendered with order-independent alpha-hash transparency and temporal anti-aliasing, producing a clean frosted-glass cluster effect. Ideal for hero sections of design tools, data visualization dashboards, product showcases, or premium brand landing pages that want a sophisticated, glassy 3D aesthetic.
usageNote: Wrap the init/animate logic inside a useEffect with a canvas ref in React or Next.js; assign renderer.domElement to the ref instead of appending to document.body. Use a cleanup function to call renderer.dispose(), composer.dispose(), and controls.dispose(). In react-three-fiber, the TAARenderPass requires manual EffectComposer wiring via useThree and a custom render loop with invalidate or frameloop='always'. No local asset paths need replacing.
constraints: Requires WebGL with support for dithered alpha-hash (GLSL discard-based transparency); TAA accumulation is GPU-intensive and may drop below 60 fps on mid-range mobile GPUs or when sampleLevel is high. OrbitControls resets TAA accumulation on every camera move, so constant interaction degrades smoothness. Not suitable for very low-end or older mobile devices.
antiPatterns: Forgetting to call composer.setSize() on window resize causes blurry or cropped output. Not disposing the PMREMGenerator or RoomEnvironment leaks GPU memory. Hardcoding window.innerWidth/innerHeight breaks embedded canvas layouts — use the container element's dimensions instead. Leaving taaRenderPass.accumulate always true causes ghosting during interaction.
accessibilityNotes: Provide a static fallback image for users with prefers-reduced-motion enabled by checking the media query and skipping the animation loop. The interactive canvas has no keyboard or screen reader affordance; add aria-hidden='true' and a visually hidden descriptive text element. Avoid relying on color alone to convey meaning since object colors are randomized.

technique: texture blending mode comparison grid with animated checkerboard background
description: A grid of image panels each rendered with a different GPU blending mode (None, Normal, Additive, Subtractive, Multiply) over a slowly scrolling tiled checkerboard background, with canvas-rendered labels beneath each panel. Ideal for design system documentation pages, shader/material editors, or any site section that needs to visually demonstrate how layered graphics or overlays will look under different compositing rules.
usageNote: Port into React/Next.js using a useEffect hook with a canvas ref: instantiate the renderer targeting the ref element rather than appending to document.body, store the animation loop ID for cleanup, and return a dispose function. Replace all local texture paths (uv_grid_opengl.jpg, sprite0.jpg/png, lensflare PNGs) with assets served from your public/ folder or a CDN URL passed in as props. The checkerboard background is generated procedurally via CanvasTexture so no external asset is needed for it.
constraints: Requires WebGL renderer; not suited to WebGPU-only pipelines without porting. Blending modes are GPU-accelerated and lightweight, so performance cost is low even on mobile. The scene is entirely static geometry so it runs well on mid-range devices. Not appropriate when you need real-time transparency sorting of many overlapping 3D objects — this is strictly 2D plane-based.
antiPatterns: Forgetting to call renderer.dispose() and texture.dispose() on unmount causing GPU memory leaks; hardcoding window.innerWidth/window.innerHeight instead of measuring the container element; not cancelling the animation loop ID on cleanup; loading textures synchronously inside the render loop instead of once at init; omitting colorSpace = THREE.SRGBColorSpace on loaded textures causing washed-out colours.
accessibilityNotes: The animation is a slow background scroll which is low-intensity but should still be paused via a CSS media query (prefers-reduced-motion) or by stopping the animation loop when the preference is detected. Provide a static screenshot or descriptive alt text for screen readers since the canvas is not inherently accessible. Labels are baked into canvas textures and invisible to assistive technology — add equivalent HTML labels if this is used in a documentation context.

technique: custom WebGL blending mode matrix visualizer
description: Displays a grid of semi-transparent textured planes against a checkered background, each rendered with a different source/destination blending factor combination, allowing interactive selection of the blend equation. Suits developer tools, design system documentation sites, or creative tool UIs that need to visually explain or let users preview compositing and layer blending modes.
usageNote: Wrap in a React useEffect with a canvas ref, or use react-three-fiber with a Canvas component. The lensflare texture must be replaced with a project-hosted asset or a procedurally generated canvas texture (as is done for the background) — the local asset path will not resolve. The GUI controls can be replaced with React state and a <select> element driving material.blendEquation updates on all materials in the array.
constraints: Requires WebGL renderer; not suitable for WebGPU-only pipelines. Renders 110+ meshes simultaneously which is moderate draw-call cost — fine on desktop but may degrade on low-end mobile GPUs. Custom blending is a WebGL 1/2 core feature so browser support is broad. The scene is static once built so GPU cost after init is low.
antiPatterns: Forgetting to call material.needsUpdate = true after changing blendEquation at runtime. Not disposing geometry and materials when the component unmounts, causing memory leaks in SPA navigation. Hardcoding window.innerWidth/innerHeight instead of using a ResizeObserver on the container element. Assuming the external texture URL will resolve — must be replaced before use.
accessibilityNotes: This is a purely visual demonstration with no interactive elements beyond the GUI. Add aria-hidden='true' to the canvas and provide a static screenshot or descriptive text alternative for screen readers. For reduced-motion users the scene is already static (no animation loop movement), so no special reduced-motion handling is needed beyond ensuring the GUI is keyboard-navigable.

technique: bump-mapped 3D mesh with spotlit shadow and orbit controls
description: A high-detail 3D mesh rendered with a grayscale bump/displacement map that simulates surface depth under a warm spotlight, producing realistic shadows and surface texture. Ideal for product showcase pages, portfolio hero sections, or luxury brand microsites where tactile material quality needs to be communicated in 3D.
usageNote: Wrap the entire init/animate block inside a useEffect with a ref-attached canvas in React or Next.js; pass the ref's current element to the renderer instead of creating a div via document.createElement. For react-three-fiber, use a <mesh> with meshPhongMaterial and a bumpMap texture loaded via useTexture. Replace the local .glb and .jpg asset paths with URLs served from your /public folder or a CDN (e.g. '/assets/model.glb' and '/assets/bumpmap.jpg'). Remove the lil-gui import and replicate the bump scale controls with your own UI state.
constraints: Requires WebGL 1 or higher; MeshPhongMaterial with bump maps and shadow maps is moderately GPU-intensive, making it unsuitable for low-end mobile devices or pages needing 60fps alongside heavy JS work. Shadow map resolution of 2048×2048 is costly; reduce to 1024 for mobile. Does not use WebGPU or WebGL2-only features so broad browser support is fine.
antiPatterns: Forgetting to call renderer.dispose() and geometry.dispose() on unmount in React causing memory leaks; hardcoding window.innerWidth/window.innerHeight instead of reading the container element's dimensions; not updating camera.aspect and calling updateProjectionMatrix on resize; leaving the animation loop running after the component unmounts by not cancelling the animation frame; forgetting to set mesh.material.needsUpdate = true after swapping the bumpMap at runtime.
accessibilityNotes: The canvas has no intrinsic accessible description; add an aria-label or visually hidden caption describing the 3D content. Respect prefers-reduced-motion by pausing or disabling orbit auto-rotation if added. Provide a static high-quality render as a fallback image for screen readers or environments where WebGL is unavailable. Keyboard navigation is not provided by OrbitControls; add keyboard event handlers or skip-links if interactivity is important.

technique: interactive 3D product configurator with HDR environment lighting and animated ground grid
description: A photorealistic 3D car model sits in a darkened studio with HDR environment reflections, spinning wheels, and a scrolling ground grid suggesting motion. Ideal for automotive e-commerce, product landing pages, or any premium goods configurator where users can orbit around and customize colors of distinct material zones (body, trim, glass).
usageNote: Wrap init() and the renderer loop inside a useEffect with a canvas ref in React/Next.js; assign renderer.domElement to the ref instead of appending to a container div. Replace local HDR and GLB asset paths with paths served from your /public folder or a CDN (e.g. /models/ferrari.glb). Color picker inputs should be replaced with React-controlled <input type='color'> elements whose onChange handlers call material.color.set(). Use react-three-fiber alternatively for a more idiomatic React approach with <Canvas> and useLoader.
constraints: Requires WebGL2 with physical material support (clearcoat, transmission); not suitable for low-end mobile GPUs. HDR environment loading adds ~1MB network cost. DRACOLoader requires WASM decoder files to be hosted separately—copy them from node_modules/three/examples/jsm/libs/draco/ to your public folder. Fullscreen canvas assumes single-page hero usage; must be resized carefully in layout contexts.
antiPatterns: Forgetting to call renderer.dispose() and controls.dispose() in the useEffect cleanup, causing memory leaks on route changes. Not hosting Draco WASM decoder files, causing silent load failures. Hardcoding window.innerWidth/window.innerHeight instead of measuring the container element, breaking embedded or split-layout use. Omitting premultipliedAlpha on the baked shadow plane causing incorrect blending.
accessibilityNotes: Provide a high-quality static image fallback (e.g. <noscript> or a CSS background) for users without WebGL or JS. Respect prefers-reduced-motion by pausing the wheel spin animation and grid scroll when the media query matches. Add an aria-label on the canvas element describing the product. Color pickers should have associated <label> elements for screen reader accessibility. Keyboard orbit controls are not natively included in OrbitControls and must be added separately.

technique: 3D mesh with switchable material channels (normal, depth, AO, displacement, velocity) and dual camera modes
description: A detailed 3D model rendered with interchangeable material visualizations — standard PBR, depth maps, normal maps, and motion velocity — viewable in both perspective and orthographic projection with orbit controls. Suits product configurators, technical visualization tools, game asset preview portals, or developer-facing 3D tooling dashboards.
usageNote: Wrap the renderer, scene, camera, and animation loop inside a React useEffect with a canvas ref (or use react-three-fiber with useFrame). Replace local OBJ and texture paths (normal.png, ao.jpg, displacement.jpg, ninjaHead_Low.obj) with paths served from your own /public directory or a CDN. Clean up by calling renderer.dispose() and controls.dispose() in the useEffect return. The GUI controls can be replaced with React state and UI components.
constraints: Requires WebGL with support for depth packing and shader materials (VelocityShader). The displacement map requires sufficient vertex density in the mesh — low-poly meshes will not show displacement correctly. Moderately expensive on mobile due to multiple material variants and displacement; limit to desktop or high-end mobile. Not suitable for use as a background element without significant geometry simplification.
antiPatterns: Forgetting to dispose all seven material variants on unmount (each must be disposed individually). Hardcoding window.innerWidth/innerHeight instead of using a ResizObserver on the canvas container. Leaving both OrbitControls instances active simultaneously — only the active camera's controls should be updated. Failing to set renderer pixel ratio, which causes blurriness on high-DPI screens.
accessibilityNotes: Provide a static image fallback (a rendered screenshot of the model) for users with prefers-reduced-motion or those on devices without WebGL support. The interactive 3D view has no keyboard orbit support by default — add OrbitControls key bindings or a visible instruction label. Screen readers receive no meaningful content from the canvas; add an aria-label describing the 3D model and an aria-hidden='true' on the canvas element.

technique: 3D model showcase with environment cubemap reflection and refraction materials
description: Three 3D head models are displayed side by side against a panoramic environment backdrop, each demonstrating a different surface material: full mirror-like reflection, glass-like refraction, and a partial metallic mix. Ideal for product configurators, luxury brand showcases, material science visualizations, or interactive 3D asset previews where users can orbit around objects.
usageNote: Wrap in a React useEffect with a canvas ref and return a cleanup function that calls renderer.dispose() and removes the animation loop. Replace the OBJLoader path with your own hosted .obj asset (e.g. in /public or via a CDN URL). Replace the cubemap texture paths with six hosted environment images (px, nx, py, ny, pz, nz). Alternatively, use react-three-fiber with <mesh> and <meshLambertMaterial envMap={...}> and @react-three/drei's <CubeCamera> or <Environment> for easier cubemap setup.
constraints: Requires WebGL with cube texture support (universally available in modern browsers). Loading a full cubemap (6 images) plus an OBJ model adds initial load time; lazy load or show a placeholder until assets resolve. Performance is moderate — three separate mesh instances with environment maps are GPU-friendly but cubemaps consume VRAM. Not recommended for low-end mobile without compressed textures.
antiPatterns: Forgetting to dispose the CubeTextureLoader textures and geometry on component unmount causes VRAM leaks. Hardcoding window.innerWidth/window.innerHeight instead of using the container's bounding rect breaks embedded or partial-page canvases. Not handling the async OBJ load completion before rendering can cause a blank frame flash. Using refractionCube without setting mapping = THREE.CubeRefractionMapping results in incorrect glass effect.
accessibilityNotes: Provide a static hero image fallback for users with prefers-reduced-motion or when WebGL is unavailable. The 3D canvas has no inherent keyboard focus or screen reader meaning — add an aria-label describing the showcased object and role='img' to the canvas element. Orbit controls should be supplemented with keyboard arrow-key rotation for accessibility.

technique: real-time dynamic cube-map reflection on metallic sphere with orbiting objects in HDR environment
description: A highly polished metallic sphere dynamically reflects its surroundings—including animated objects orbiting around it—against a photorealistic HDR environment background.
